description: Within the UCI BioSci foundational theme of MIND | BODY | WORLD, the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology focuses on the WORLD and how the MIND and BODY are embedded in this context. Our department studies the molecular basis of how organisms adapt to the natural world over evolutionary time, and how the resultant biological diversity in organismal function affects present-day ecological processes. EEB faculty study questions pertinent at a variety of levels of biological organization, from molecular aspects of evolution to organismal physiology and the ecology of terrestrial, freshwater and ocean ecosystems. We seek to train a diverse student body for successful scientific careers by providing a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive environment for department members.

name: Department of Economics
description: The PhD program in Economics at UC Irvine prepares students for careers in academia, government, and the private sector. The program typically enrolls 15-20 students each year.  The expected time to degree is 5 years.  Students are admitted to the PhD program with full funding for five years.

name: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) has two key goals: to advance the minds of future leaders by providing the finest education to our students and consistently meet industry needs by developing cutting-edge technology. Our faculty believes that engineering plays an integral role in the modernization of society by leading the development of tools and devices that benefit humankind and improve quality of life.

name: Department of English Ph.D. Program
description: The Ph.D. program in English at UCI is the #1 department for literary and critical theory nationally (US News and World Report). The research and teaching of department faculty represents and cuts across a range of fields, historical periods, and methodological approaches. Our graduates have gone on to faculty positions at a range of nationally ranked colleges and universities, including, in recent years, the University of Michigan, Tulane, Rice, Clemson, BYU, and Connecticut College.Many of our PhD faculty and students participate jointly in collaborative, interdisciplinary research clusters and reading groups. Some groups currently active include The Center for Early Cultures, the Culture and Capital Center, Medieval Devysings, Poetics | History | Theory, the Queer Theory Reading Group, and the Rhetoric Reading Group. Our Ph.D. program allows students to customize their study and research around their own intellectual interests. Students can also take seminars in other programs and departments, and can receive interdisciplinary certificates in Asian American studies, Chicano/Latino Studies, Critical Theory, Gender and Sexuality Studies, Latin American Studies, Medical Humanities, Rhetoric and Composition, and Visual Studies.All admitted students receive a multi-year funding package, including a range of teaching opportunities. Students may enter the graduate program in English with either a B.A. or an M.A. degree. In either case, the first two years are spent taking courses, completing the language requirement, and writing the M.A. paper. In the third year, students select two or three fields of study for their qualifying exams--exam lists are developed by the student in consultation with their advisor and are intended to help the student build expertise and confidence toward a future dissertation. After successfully completing the qualifying examination, students write a dissertation under the supervision of a three-person dissertation committee, which they select.

name: Department of Environmental and Occupational Health (Environmental Health, M.S./Ph.D.)
description: Department of Environmental and Occupational HealthThe mission of the Department of Environmental and Occupational Health (DEOH) in the Program in Public Health (PPH) is to conduct interdisciplinary research and teaching across the fields of exposure science, toxicology, risk assessment, epidemiology, urban health, climate change, natural disasters, environmental health disparity, and related disciplines, to elucidate how environmental exposures in home, community, and occupational settings influence human health and the development and progression of human disease, with the aim of preventing human illness and disability and promoting well-being. In pursuit of this mission, the DEOH will focus on integrative and transdisciplinary health research using the three pillars of science: basic, clinical, and population science. Research with particular emphases on assessing exposures to and health risks from environmental and occupational factors include, but are not limited to contaminants in ambient air, water, food, and soil; green space and the built environment; radiation; noise; temperature; work organization; and community and workplace stressors.

name: Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics (Epidemiology, M.S./Ph.D.)
description: Department of Epidemiology and BiostatisticsThe mission of the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics is to improve population health through research, education, community engagement, and translating discoveries into practice.Epidemiology is a quantitative, data-driven discipline that uses rigorous methods to collect, analyze, and interpret health-related data in human populations. Epidemiologists use this information to examine the distribution and determinants of disease and to apply this information to develop disease prevention strategies to improve population health.Epidemiology is an exciting field that not only develops and applies rigorous epidemiology methods, but also draws on other scientific disciplines, including biostatistics, informatics, genomics, biology, economics, social and behavioral sciences. Welcome to the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics in the Program in Public Health at UC Irvine.

name: Department of Gender and Sexuality Studies
description: Since its inception in 1975 as the center of feminist scholarship and teaching at UC Irvine, the Department of Gender & Sexuality Studies has been dedicated to the interdisciplinary study of gender and sexuality in their complex articulations with race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, and socio-economic class. The Department draws critical attention to "gender" and "sexuality" as concept-terms that necessarily invoke multiple systems of oppression, inequality and privilege, and which engender various forms of embodiment, desire, subjectivity, knowledge and politics. We look at masculinities and femininities not as natural, pre-given facts lodged in a clear-cut binary system of biological difference, but as products of specific cultural, political and economic processes.

name: Department of Health, Society, and Behavior & Department of Population Health and Disease Prevention (Public Health, Ph.D.)
description: Department of Health, Society, and BehaviorOur department is comprised of a dynamic array of faculty with diverse backgrounds in public health and related fields in the social and biological sciences. Our faculty primarily has expertise in the areas of health behavior, social determinants of health, social epidemiology, health disparities and health equity, community-based research, biobehavioral health, and health communication. Our core values include investigating the etiology of health behavior related processes and outcomes, the dynamics of marginalized populations, community-based research and practice, the creation of theoretically-informed health interventions and their respective evaluation studies, health communication, and biobehavioral health. The research, teaching, and practice interests of our faculty primarily address the explication of complex pathways linking social, cultural, and biological factors with health, with an emphasis on social determinants of health, social epidemiology, social disparities in health and health equity. We are poised to address complex health issues at the local, global, regional, and national levels given the multidisciplinary research and practice expertise of our faculty.Department of Population Health and Disease PreventionThe mission of the Department of Population Health and Disease Prevention (DPHDP) is to create, integrate, and translate population-based knowledge into preventive strategies to reduce the societal burden of human disease and disability through excellence in interdisciplinary research, education, and public service. The DPHDP was established in 2008 as the first department within the PPH to provide a formal academic structure for the multidisciplinary pursuit of a public health mission and administration of degree programs. This forward-thinking strategy promoted excellence in cross-disciplinary research and practice, expansion of degree programs, and growth of the public health student population. In 2020 the DPHDP reached a critical size and junction whereby faculty could branch out to populate complementary new departments with more disciplinary focus. The DPHDP looks forward to continued growth within the future School of Population and Public Health.

name: Department of History
description: The Department History is designed to develop critical intelligence and to foster an awareness of ourselves and our world through the study of the past. The Department presents a variety of approaches to history, and each emphasizes basic disciplinary skills: weighing evidence, constructing logical arguments, and exploring the role of theory in historical analysis and human action.

name: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
description: We are an interdisciplinary and enthusiastic group of faculty and staff who are firmly committed to the success of our students and programs. The field of materials science and engineering sits at the intersection of chemistry, physics and engineering, with increasing expansion into mathematics, computing, machine learning, manufacturing and imaging, plus economics, sustainability and public policy. MSE is the field that enables all other areas of engineering by understanding – and therefore creating – new and exciting materials that enable faster computers, cleaner energy, more efficient automobiles and airplanes, stronger and longer-lasting hip implants and so much more!

name: Department of Philosophy
description: UCI's Philosophy Department is committed to providing students a well-rounded graduate education, including central areas of contemporary philosophy and a solid foundation in the history of philosophy. Those with interests in mathematics, the natural sciences, or the social sciences are encouraged to take courses in Logic and Philosophy of Science and to include LPS faculty members on their dissertation committees. Our cooperative two-track program provides students the benefits of faculty expertise in a host of areas.

name: Department of Physiology & Biophysics
description: The mission of the UCI Department of Physiology & Biophysics is to provide an environment which provides leadership and excellence in teaching and research. Biomedical/basic science research programs are conducted to evaluate and contribute to the medical scientific knowledge of the disciplines of physiology and biophysics. The educational program encompasses graduate students, medical students, undergraduate students and faculty participation in training preeminent scholars and postgraduate researchers.

name: Department of Sociology
description: The graduate program offers broad training in sociology, with several areas of concentrated expertise: education; family, life course, and sexualities; global inequality and change; immigration; population; organizations, occupations, and labor; social inequality: race/ethnicity, gender, and class/stratification; social movements and political sociology; social networks; organizations, occupations, and labor; and the study of democracy.  We are committed to theoretically informed and empirically grounded scholarship.  We welcome multidisciplinary pursuits, forging links with other units on the campus and beyond.  We also embrace a broad range of methods – including ethnography, experiments, formal modeling, historical-comparative analysis, and surveys – to pursue answers to questions of substantive and theoretical importance.  The program offers both MA and PhD degrees, although the latter is emphasized.Resources for graduate students extend well beyond the department.  UCI's nationally-recognized program in Criminology, Law, and Society offers opportunities for study in these areas, and members of the department have close ties with the Institute for Mathematical Behavioral Sciences; the Center for the Study of Democracy; Center for Organizational Research; the Center in Global Peace and Conflict Studies; the Center in Demographic and Social Analysis; the Center in Law, Society, and Culture; and the Center for Immigration, Population, and Public Policy.  All provide interested students with additional research communities and opportunities. Students have taken courses with faculty in these programs and from faculty with related interests in other social science fields, including anthropology and political science.By design and disposition, our faculty is committed to working collaboratively with graduate students.  Our graduate program is constructed to help students move from being consumers of research to being producers of important, and published, work.  In addition to numerous opportunities for collaboration with faculty members, students must, by the end of their second year, produce independent research targeted for journal publication.  Students who take advantage of these opportunities have good success in finding professional employment.  Recent graduates have accepted tenure-track positions at both small colleges and major research universities, including University of California-Los Angeles, Tulane University, the University of Washington, the University of Massachusetts-Amherst, and the University of California-Riverside.  Current graduate students have won external research funding and published a wide array of journal articles and book chapters. Given the department's ongoing growth and enhanced national visibility, we are confident our students will continue to do well on the job market.

name: Design at UCI
description: Design at UCI is a community for designers of all skill levels and backgrounds. We provide the resources and space for students to innovate, create, and ultimately grow as designers. Through community, education, and collaboration, we strive to spark and foster creativity in our members and throughout the UCI community.

name: Diabetes Link at UCI
description: The mission of this organization is to create a supportive and stigma-reducing space for students, faculty, staff, and campus affiliates to learn about the complexities of managing diabetes

name: Dialogue Society
description: Guided by the belief that there is always a better version of oneself, Dialogue Society aims to enrich the lives of communities. Our purpose is to educate the community through meaningful dialogues on healthy, purposeful and mindful living—free from promoting political affiliations or religious beliefs—to discover what inspires us towards personal development. We move forward by the motto of "Dialogue. Discover. Develop."

name: DigiFilm Society at UCI
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide students with events catered to enriching their knowledge of filmmaking and expose themselves to professionals working in the industry.  We also strive to connect students with resources and each other in order to promote filmmaking at UCI.

name: Disability and Neurodiversity Alliance Plus
description: The Disability and Neurodiversity Alliance Plus is a support and advocacy group of undergraduate students at UC Irvine. We are led by students with disabilities including people who identify as d/Deaf, autistic, and allies of people with disabilities, represented by the “Plus” in our name. We aim to make our club a safe space to destigmatize disability identity and create opportunities for self-advocacy and mutual aid. DNA+ will further raise awareness of accessibility while also creating a campus culture supportive of students with disabilities.

name: Disability Services Center
description: Eliminate, Eradicate, and Obliterate Stereotypical Thinking about Disability.• Provides free and confidential services that are open to all UCI students with disabilities, including international and undocumented students.• Strives to create a culture of inclusion and access in all aspects of student life at UCI.• Challenges and seeks to eliminate stereotypes and myths about disability.

name: Diverse Abilities Inclusion & Support for Youth
description: Diverse Abilities Inclusion & Support for Youth aims at raising awareness about the importance of inclusivity as well as the obstacles that children with diverse disabilities face. In order to achieve this, DAISY works alongside children with various temporary and chronic disabilities, including cognitive and physical conditions, to help improve their quality of life, inspire them to reach their full potentials, and offer a strong network of peers and support.

name: Division of Career Pathways
description: The Division of Career Pathways educates and engages UCI students and alumni to realize their career potential. We do this by:• Coordinating with the campus community in the professional development of students.• Providing students and alumni with tools and support to attain their career goals.• Delivering exceptional customer service to the employer community while recognizing individual recruiting needs.

name: Division of Teaching Excellence and Innovation (DTEI)
description: The Division of Teaching Excellence and Innovation (DTEI) is dedicated to partnering with faculty, graduate students, and postdocs to maximize students' academic success. We accomplish this by cultivating exceptional learning environments across campus through pedagogical development opportunities focused on integrating innovative, evidence-based teaching practices. DTEI's goals align with the Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning (OVPTL) and Pillar 2 and 4 of the UCI Strategic Plan:1. Enhance pedagogical training for faculty, graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff by providing and developing certification, teaching assistant training, and fellowship programs.2. Partner with campus researchers to collect and disseminate data on evidence-based practices that the campus community can use to improve student success.3. Promote the effective utilization of digital technologies by the UCI community to foster teaching innovation and enhance student face-to-face and online learning.    4. Coordinate efforts to systematically align campus learning environments with current and emerging educational practices to maximize student success.5. Evaluate the impact of DTEI programs and campus learning environments on both students and instructors, utilizing assessment data to further improve teaching and learning on campus.

name: Division of Undergraduate Education (DUE)
description: DUE provides leadership, advocacy and coordination for campus initiatives that impact undergraduate education and enhance student access and retention. Working with faculty, the Academic Senate, academic support staff and others, DUE units deliver a wide variety of academic programs and services that support undergraduate teaching and learning campuswide.

name: Doctors Without Borders at UCI
description: We aim to inform and raise awareness among the broader community about global conflicts and ways individuals can support these efforts, whether through fundraising, education, or resource provision. Additionally, our commitment extends to assisting individuals irrespective of their gender, political beliefs, or religious affiliation.

name: Dragon Boat at UC Irvine
description: Dragon Boat at UC Irvine is a team that competes at dragon boat festivals, racing against other college teams and non-college teams. Dragon boat is a sport consisting of twenty paddlers in a long canoe shaped boat, paddling simultaneously. We are heading into our 21st year of existence and have races in San Francisco; Tempe, AZ; Long Beach; San Diego; and even Vancouver. We are a team that strives to exceed expectations in our training and competition. Along with training, our team aims to build strong bonds and create a big family. With this sense of family and competition, we strive to represent UCI at the best of our ability at every race.

name: Drainers at UCI
description: At Drainers at UCI, our mission is to foster a safe, inclusive, and vibrant community centered around a shared passion for underground music. We aim to bring together students who seek connection through niche genres and emerging artists, providing a space where they can discover new sounds, express themselves, and build meaningful relationships. In the short term, we strive to cultivate a supportive environment for fans to meet and engage with one another. In the long term, we aspire to grow a lasting network of friendships rooted in a love for underground music and authentic connection.

name: DreamCatchers at UCI
description: DreamCatchers at UCI develops students into compassionate leaders through fostering intergenerational connections between students and older adults, particularly those who are in hospice. These connections are created through acts of service, primarily by fulfilling end-of-life Dreams for hospice patients.

name: Drive Sober Orange County
description: Young adults are more isolated and misinformed about the psychologies and substances that alter them now more than ever. The dichotomy of drug use lies in the fact that while we become more open to substance use, its consequences multiply in severity. Now, more than ever, discussing intervention methods that provide factual data and real-world improvements is critical.This student-led organization promotes safe driving, safe alcohol and substance use habits, and safety among young adults, specifically those within Orange County. The organization strives to promote these ideals through guidance, advocacy, awareness, and intervention against impaired driving.

name: D¡tto (K-Pop Dance Class Club)
description: D¡tto is in reference to the transforming copy-cat Pokémon and composition by NJZ (a K-pop group), building a connection to our mission of allowing students to become whoever they want to be and providing a shared space where people can share passion, creativity, and cultural exchange. D¡tto aims to provide new experiences to students wanting to learn how to dance or admire Korean culture. Therefore, this club is built to encourage members to learn, move, and grow together.

name: Earth System Science Club
description: ESSC is an academic and social club that focuses on providing guidance, professional development opportunities, and a place for students to meet others interested in environmental careers. All majors are welcome!

name: EarthReps - UCI Housing Sustainability
description: EarthReps is a student training and community building internship for undergraduate on-campus residents offering education, skills, and hands-on experiences broadly related to sustainability. EarthReps serve as sustainability ambassadors in student housing. The program aims to train emerging young leaders, expand campus awareness of sustainability, and build community among students, staff, and faculty. EarthReps receive training in substantive sustainability issues as well as skills for initiating essential conversations among peers, planning hall activities, and other community building approaches.

name: East African Student Association
description: EASA’s mission is to foster a strong, inclusive community for East African students at UCI by celebrating our cultures, uplifting underrepresented voices, and creating a space where students feel seen, supported, and empowered. We aim to connect students through shared identity and experience, and promote cultural pride through events, dialogue, and mentorship.

name: Echolalia: Undergraduate Literary Journal (formerly Echolalia)
description: Echolalia: Undergraduate Literary Journal's purpose is to create a safe and non-discriminatory environment for all students of University California, Irvine to express their literary voices in an accessible publication. Echolalia will be working to make a difference by providing a resourceful outlet and promoting interests in literature, and creative, as well as academic writing by means of disseminating a publication.

name: Ecology and Evolutionary Club at UCI
description: The purpose of EEB Club is to create a community for those involved in the EEB major or interested in EEB. We will highlight community and volunteer events, resources for students, connect with faculty and peers etc.

name: Egyptian Student Association at UCI
description: To provide a community filled with Egyptians or people interested in Egyptian culture. To create a space for Egyptians to meet one another and to create connections here at UCI.

name: End Overdose at UCI
description: Our mission is to make resources that prevent opioid overdoses readily available to the UCI community and beyond, and to raise public awareness of drug-related deaths and how they can be prevented.

name: ENG Office of Outreach, Access, and Inclusion
description: OAI is an office within the Henry Samueli School of Engineering created in 2014 to recruit, retain, and graduate talented students from historically excluded populations who are currently underrepresented in Engineering.

name: Engineering Student Council (ESC)
description: It is the mission of the Engineering Student Council (ESC) at UC Irvine to be a liaison between undergraduate engineering students and the faculty, staff, and administration of The Henry Samueli School of Engineering. ESC serves as the umbrella organization for other Engineering Student Organizations to promote cooperation and build relationships among students. We create networking and research opportunities for students by coordinating events with other organizations, faculty members, and corporations across Southern California. As student leaders, we envision and advocate for the educational, social, and professional advancement of the engineering community.

name: Engineering Undergraduate Student Affairs
description: The Engineering Undergraduate Student Affairs office provides a full range of academic counseling services to undergraduate students in our 11 Engineering majors and 2 Engineering minors as well as advising for students interested in changing their major into Engineering.Students are not assigned to specific academic counselors and are free to see any available counselor or Peer Advisors (by appointment or on a walk-in basis) during the office’s open hours.

name: Engineers for a Sustainable World at UCI - ESW
description: Engineers for a Sustainable World (ESW) at UCI is a chapter of a non-profit organization that is committed to building a greener world and welcomes students of all majors (engineering and non engineering) that believe in need to improve our environment. ESW focuses on designing sustainable engineering projects, professional development and educating members on sustainability. Our events include alumni panels, networking opportunities, tours to facilities, and our projects range from building solar charging stations, cultivating algae for bio-fuel, to designing piezoelectric objects. This organization would be a great way to get more students involved with hands-on projects and spread awareness about sustainability.

name: Engineers Without Borders at UCI
description: The purpose of EWB-UCI shall reflect and support the values and mission of Engineers Without Borders-USA: “to partner with disadvantaged communities to improve their quality of life through implementation of environmentally sound and economically sustainable engineering projects, while developing internationally responsible engineering students.”

name: English Majors Association at UCI
description: The English Majors' Association (EMA) works to bring together students and faculty to build a sense of community within the English Department and a support system for current undergraduate students. Although the club is primarily aimed towards students in the English major/minor, we also welcome students from the Literary Journalism and Comparative Literature programs, as well as anyone who is interested in discussing literature! EMA holds regular weekly meetings as well as quarterly events such as Book Swaps, Poetry Events, Open Mic Nights, Research Presentations, and Game Nights.

name: Entertainment and Sports Law Society
description: The Entertainment and Sports Law Society is a student-run organization focused on incorporating business and legal studies involving music, film, fashion, video games, sports, and other industries of interest. Our organization hosts speaker presentations, social events, and provides networking opportunities in an effort to circulate industry information and contacts within the entertainment and sports law sector. The organization will also create a publication informing the UCI Law community about current issues and legal decisions affecting the industry at large.

name: Environmental Law Society at University of California Irvine School of Law
description: We are a group of student activists eager to learn about local, national, and global environmental challenges. Our hope is to explore the wide variety of opportunities for environmental lawyers and policymakers to enact change. ELS also aims to bring together community leaders interested in all types and scales of environmental issues. Our events will address issues surrounding environmental justice, the climate crisis, biodiversity, and habitat loss. We plan to host speakers, inform students of job opportunities, network with other student groups at UCI and around the country, help students connect with professionals in environmental law, conduct greening activities, and participate in advocacy campaigns.

name: Eta Kappa Nu
description: IEEE-Eta Kappa Nu is the student honor society of IEEE and is dedicated to encouraging and recognizing excellence in the IEEE-designated fields of interest. Members consist of students, alumni, and other professionals who have demonstrated exceptional academic and professional accomplishments. Student members are selected on the basis of scholastic standing, character, and leadership. Through a variety of service programs and leadership training, student members develop lifelong skills that earmark them for prominent positions in industry and academia. Members are much better prepared for the post-college world and are especially valuable and attractive to employers. They are recognized as extremely capable, both technically and professionally.  After graduation, members continue their involvement through their university chapters, volunteering for IEEE-HKN committees and receiving information on IEEE-HKN activities.  To further recognize excellence, IEEE-HKN conducts award programs to recognize professional leaders, exceptional educators, outstanding students, young engineering professionals, outstanding chapters, and effective faculty advisors.  For more than 100 years, Eta Kappa Nu has embraced excellence. In the years ahead, IEEE-HKN will continue to reinvent itself to meet the needs of its members, the institutions they serve, and our overall society.

name: Eta Sigma Phi at UCI
description: This organization exists to develop and promote interest in classical study among the students of colleges and universities; to promote closer relationships among students who are interested in classical study, including inter-campus relationships; to engage generally in an effort to stimulate interest in classical study, and in the languages, literature, history, and art of ancient Greece and Rome.

name: Euphonic Video Game Ensemble at UCI
description: To provide musicians, artists, and other video game/enthusiasts a safe space & creative outlet to express their love for their favorite media.

name: F1Tenth at UCI
description: Educate members on the principles of autonomous vehicles while also designing algorithms and competing the F1Tenth car at robotics competitions.

name: FADA Film Arts Drama Alliance Network at UCI
description: FADA is an organization dedicated to networking student filmmakers and promoting collaborative filmmaking. We sponsor weekly ZOTFILM production meetings, where club members can enjoy producing short-films with other members of the UCI film community. All of this will culminate in our student-run film festival and celebration, ZOTFEST, at the end of the year.

name: Family Resource Center
description: The Family Resource Center will provide practical support services and a welcoming, sustainable community gathering space where families can connect and thrive.

name: Fashion and Sneakers at UCI -FS at UCI
description: FSUCI aims to make fashion more than just a hobby. FSUCI celebrates fashion as a powerful form of self-identity and is committed to building a place where students creatively express themselves in any way they wish. Members can share their experiences and tastes in fashion and feel uplifted by club members regardless of differing opinions in the fashion community through hands-on experiences and community-driven events that incorporate fashion as a medium. Additionally, we aim to introduce undergraduate students to career pathways within the fashion and apparel industry.

name: Fashion Collective at UCI (formerly Anteater Atelier Fashion Club)
description: Providing creatives across UCI a platform to work collectively towards building community and defining the future of fashion.

name: Federal Bar Association (FBA) Law School Student Chapter
description: We are committed to fostering the highest standards of professionalism and legal competence among law students at UCI. Our mission is to provide opportunities for professional development, networking, and service to the community. We aim to bridge the gap between students and the federal legal profession by facilitating meaningful interactions with practitioners, judges, and public servants in the federal system. We strive to enhance understanding of federal law and the federal legal system, promote the welfare and interests of law students, and contribute to the advancement of justice under the law.

name: Federalist Society [The] at UCI
description: Founded in 1982, the Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies is a group of conservatives and libertarians dedicated to reforming the current legal order. We are committed to the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be. The Society seeks to promote awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities and welcomes all interested in exploring these principles.

name: Fencing Club at UCI
description: Fencing Club at UCI competes at the collegiate level against other schools in Southern California. We encourage everyone interested in fencing to join us for practice. We welcome beginners and experienced fencers alike. Equipment and instruction are provided. Drop by and check us out!

name: Fighting Gamers at UCI
description: FightingGamers@UCI (FG@UCI) is a student organization on the campus of the University of California, Irvine (UCI) for people who have an interest in fighting games. What began as a small club for UCI students, FG@UCI is now a community comprised of SoCal's most passionate fighting gamers. Our goal is to host gatherings where fighting gamers can meet, play, and grow with others. We accomplish this by providing a positive and enriching environment through our weekly sessions and special events, all held at UCI and open to the public. We strive to provide our members with resources necessary to enable their passion for fighting games. Weekly meetings take place on Tuesdays at the UCI Esports Arena from 6:30 PM to midnight. Feel free to stop by, and join our Discord for club updates! https://discord.gg/xHhSeaQ

name: Figure Skating Club at UCI
description: The purpose of Figure Skating Club at UCI is to promote the sport of figure skating within the Irvine community and provide ways for its members to progress in and enjoy the sport as a team and as individuals. We are committed to community service and outreach and seek to build a community of skaters who train together, encourage and support each other, and celebrate each others' accomplishments.

name: Filipino Catholic Community - Liwanag
description: Our mission is to build a humble community of God, united with the Catholic Church, to foster the spiritual growth of young adults through our Marian devotion and response to the Holy Spirit. Liwanag strives to become disciples of Jesus, servants to servants, and a light to all.

name: Filipinx Undergraduate Scientist-Engineers In an Organized Network (FUSION) (formerly Filipinos Unifying Scientist-Engineers In an Organized Network)
description: FUSION exists to provide a community that fosters the personal and professional growth of members through the facets of the science & engineering field and Filipino culture.

name: Film and Media Studies
description: Film and Media Studies focuses on the histories, theories, aesthetics, and cultural meanings of film, television, video games, digital platforms, and other media. We offer students strong liberal arts training to analyze and make sense of the complex and ever-evolving media landscape. Our award-winning faculty are engaged in innovative research on topics including video games, television, critical race studies, gender and sexuality studies, post-colonial studies, and other areas; our courses give our students access to this cutting-edge research. In our production and screenwriting courses, students get hands-on experience creating short films, television pilots, webisodes, computer games, and other visual media to deepen their understanding of how media work.

name: Film and Media Studies PhD
description: UC Irvine's PhD program in Film and Media Studies offers students the opportunity to study and develop original research on film, television, and digital media. Rooted in the Humanities, we focus on interpreting the histories and theories of media and their cultural contexts.

name: Financial Literacy Association - FLA
description: The goal of the Financial Literacy Association shall be to aid undergraduate University of California, Irvine students to make better and more informed decisions regarding the use and management of money.

name: First Generation First Quarter Challenge
description: The FGFQ program offers opportunities for Social Science students to succeed in their first year at the university. FGFQ serves students who were the first in their family to attend college. Our program was developed by Social Science students, staff, and faculty who were also the first in their family to attend college. They know firsthand what it takes to succeed at UCI and are eager to offer their support, guidance and friendship to other first generation students as they settle into the university.

name: First Generation Professionals Program at UCI Law
description: FGP seeks to foster an inclusive UCI Law community that supports first-generation, economically underrepresented and/or non-traditional law students as well as their support networks including partners, family, and communities. FGP is an organization that not only provides a shared space to reflect on these experiences, but also fosters academic success, self-care and personal support for our members' personal well-being and professional aptitude.  FGP members further seeks to build on UCI Law's goal of building a diverse law school student body, and offer programming that creates a more diverse law pipeline. FGP is centered on principles that support these goals rather than a single identity.

name: Fishing Club at UCI
description: The Fishing Club at UCI’s mission is to facilitate and foster the sport/hobby of fishing among the UCI student populace and the importance of fish and wildlife conservation. This club is also intended to be an outlet that readily provides fishing opportunities and community space for those familiar with and new to the sport and hobby.

name: Flying Samaritans at UCI
description: This organization is an undergraduate-run branch of the Southern California Chapter of The Flying Samaritans, a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. The UCI chapter is not an independent 501(c)(3) entity and operates under the oversight of The Flying Samaritans. We are committed to facilitating the service efforts of The Flying Samaritans, Inc., a registered non-profit corporation. Students, physicians, dentists, optometrists, pilots, and other healthcare practitioners travel monthly to medical clinics located throughout Mexico to provide free, quality healthcare to those who would otherwise lack access.Healthcare is provided to the people living in the rural areas outside of Tecate, Mexico in our student-run clinic, Clinica Jose Lemus Lopez Heroes del Desierto Mexico in El Testerazo. At our clinic, our members have the opportunity to assist in administrating, translating, and taking vital signs. Furthermore, students are able to witness the clinic flow and view different aspects of primary care from: intake, assessment, diagnosis, and discharge. Our members can experience healthcare and immerse themselves in another culture firsthand, both of which are incredibly educational and rewarding.

name: Food Recovery Network UCI
description: In September 2011 Food Recovery Network (FRN) was founded as a student group at the University of Maryland. Today, we're the largest student movement fighting against food waste and hunger and have recovered and donated more than 3.9 million pounds of food that otherwise would have gone to waste. That's more than 3.2 million meals that's gone to those in need. It is also more than 6.8 million pounds of carbon dioxide prevented from reaching the atmosphere.

name: Forte Theater Company
description: Women and minorities are still sorely absent from directing, producing, stage management, and administrative positions in the theater and entertainment industry. Forte Theater Company pledges to prioritize, encourage, and value the involvement of women and minorities not only in the selection of performance material, but in decision-making and leadership positions. FTC will be a space for women and minorities to gain leadership and artistic experience that will equip them with life, work, and social skills to support their goals and success long after UCI graduation. Club structures like the Creative Committee, Communications and Value Officer, and quarterly Feedback Forums ensure diversity in leadership and decision making, constant upkeep of club values, and consistent opportunities for self-reflection and accountability. FTC will provide more performance opportunities for underclassmen and underrepresented students. FTC plans to have at least one freshman-only performance opportunity per year, helping UCI first-years gain performance experience that can otherwise be very difficult to find in UCI’s competitive theater program. This will ease the transition into collegiate theater for drama majors, and provide opportunities for freshman students of all majors to connect with peers, express themselves, and expand their comfort zones. FTC plans to perform student-written work, elevate underrepresented stories and progressive revivals, encourage participation of non-arts majors, and increase connectivity between dance, drama, and music students at UCI. FTC pledges to have at least one performance with content voted on through Activity Elections. This will allow the UC Irvine community both inside and outside the club to share what work they’d like to see and representation gaps we could help fill.FTC also seeks to create more approachable and accessible non-audition creative events like open mics and workshops. UC Irvine is a high-level and competitive institution, especially in drama spaces, and this can be intimidating, especially to minorities, transfer students, non-drama majors, and first-year students. Our commitment to inclusion, accessibility, and prioritizing collaborative art creation over competition will make FTC a unique and invaluable environment for countless UC Irvine students.

name: Free Clinic Project
description: Our mission is to provide quality patient centered health care to the underserved community within Orange County, with an emphasis on educating future healthcare professionals and increasing awareness of the health care disparity through our continual research.

name: French and Francophone Club at UCI
description: The mission of the French and Francophone Club at UCI is to connect students who have an interest and or passion in the French language and francophone culture at UCI. The French and Francophone Club at UCI encourages students of all backgrounds to learn more about the francophone world.

name: Furries at UCI
description: Furries at UCI is a social club for UCI students within the furry fandom, a community that takes interest in anthropomorphic animal characters. We aim to create a safe environment for students to connect with others within the furry fandom, foster friendships, receive support from peers, and freely express their creativity and personality through unique animal characters. We host regular meetings for club members to socialize and play games, as well as provide resources for local furry events.

name: Game Design & Interactive Media
description: UCI's Game Design and Interactive Media program prepares students to be innovative designers, developers, and industry leaders. Taught by internationally recognized faculty and industry experts, the program's unique two-year foundation includes hands-on courses in worldbuilding, game design and development, game programming, and game studies. Students then pursue advanced coursework that culminates in a two-quarter capstone project supported by industry mentors. Electives in advanced game design and development, programming, storytelling, games entrepreneurship, and the cultural aspects of games offer students the chance to build a portfolio that reflects their individual interests and career goals. The program explores both established and emerging platforms, including AR/VR, tabletop, and mobile. Located in Silicon Beach, our students benefit from access to industry partners like Blizzard, Riot, Electronic Arts, Obsidian Entertainment, Age of Learning, Disney, Tencent, and the Cartoon Network.

name: Gamma Phi Beta (Gamma Phi)
description: Gamma Phi Beta was founded November 11, 1874 at Syracuse University. Our mission is to promote the highest form of womanhood through education, social life and service to humanity. Our founders, Helen M. Dodge, Francis E. Haven, E. Adeline Curtis and Mary A. Bingham started this organization to foster a nurturing environment that provides women the opportunity to achieve their potential.

name: Gavin Herbert Eye Institute
description: The mission of UC Irvine's Gavin Herbert Eye Institute and Department of Ophthalmology at UC Irvine's School of Medicine is to develop innovative technologies, clinical solutions and educational programs that enhance visual health and performance for people in Orange County, the nation and the world.This mission will be accomplished in cooperation with medical professionals, industry and our community by:Giving patients the most advanced medical and surgical eye careEducating the finest ophthalmologists and researchers in the nationPushing the boundaries of eye care research in collaboration with the medical industry and the community.

name: General Chemistry Peer Mentoring at UCI
description: Our mission is to provide free guidance to UCI undergraduates seeking reliable academic support from peers, primarily in general chemistry coursework. We also aim to encourage and mentor undergraduates who are interested in general chemistry.

name: Genetic Counseling Special Interest Group at UCI - GCSIG
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide students with the opportunity to learn more about the field of genetic counseling. Additionally, students will gain first-hand experience discussing genetic disorders, speaking and making connections with different kinds of genetic counselors, and learn about different graduate programs available for the field.

name: Girl Gains
description: Our mission is to promote female weight lifting while empowering all gender-identities to feel strong and beautiful in a judgement-free community. Whether you're a dedicated gym goer or a curious beginner, Girl Gains is here to support you in every stage of your fitness journey.

name: Global Business Brigades
description: Global Business Brigades is a secular, student-operated volunteer organization that partners with Global Brigades, an international nonprofit organization, to empower communities without proper access to economic resources in Ghana, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Greece. This empowerment involves partnering with such communities to provide sustainable financial opportunities and assistance after a holistic review of each community’s specific needs, with the ultimate goal of community ownership of a sustainable healthcare system. Global Business Brigades is the business-centric chapter within the organization, targeting the countries Honduras, Panama, and Greece.

name: Global Connect @ UC Irvine
description: Global Connect is an original educational partnership developed by UCI's School of Social Sciences to enrich California's secondary school curriculum in international studies. This is accomplished by translating current university-level concepts and knowledge into a curriculum that is age appropriate for high school and middle school students. The global studies knowledge gap in our public schools is a critical problem that needs a flexible and immediate response. Students need lessons they can relate to as global citizens that will affect how they see themselves in the world. The study of worldwide issues through Global Connect establishes an environment that creates responsible global citizens and encourages young learners to pursue higher education. Global Connect builds a bridge to the world for our nation's secondary school students.

name: Global Dental Brigades at UCI
description: Global Dental Brigades is an international movement of students and healthcare professionals working alongside local communities and staff to implement sustainable health systems. We work in remote, rural, and under resourced communities in Honduras, Panama, Guatemala, Belize, Ghana, and Greece, which would otherwise have limited to no access to health care.

name: Global Health Research Education And Translation Club
description: Global Health Research, Education, and Translation (GHREAT) is dedicated to promoting awareness of global health issues in the UCI community through the analysis of news, trends, and research literature. We place an emphasis on global health research and communication, completing one research project per academic year. By creating an open and engaging forum for the discussion of global health topics, members will increase their understanding of global health issues both at home and abroad through an interdisciplinary lens.

name: Global Medical Brigades [The]
description: The Global Medical Brigades (GMB) nonprofit partners with communities in Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Nicaragua, Greece, and Ghana to form and staff free clinics for populations without proper access to healthcare. During the spring or summer of each year, our club travels to one of these clinics and/or works with clinic staff during a virtual "telebrigade." Before these programs, our club at UCI works to raise funds for the clinics and programming and learns about international healthcare. Although the format for any given program depends on members' interests and finances, participants are guaranteed opportunities to shadow doctors, learn about international treatments and medications, and work directly with patients in a variety of specialties. Through funding the in-person or virtual programs, our club directly supports GMB international clinics and empowers communities to build sustainable healthcare systems.

name: Global Medical Missions Alliance @ UCI (GMMA)
description: Global Medical Missions Alliance is a Christian healthcare organization that strives to fulfill the Great Commission of Jesus Christ by equipping the next generation of future healthcare leaders and professionals. It provides a unique community and fellowship among peers and mentors committed to medical missions and healing ministries. There are many opportunities for training, networking, short-term local and abroad medical missions.

name: Global Medical Training at UCI
description: The purpose of Global Medical Training as an organization is to provide aid and healthcare to underserved communities around the world. Established in 2008 as the third chapter of GMT within the UC system, we are a humanitarian organization for students of premedical, pre-pharmacy, pre-dental, and all other pre-health professions focusing on serving vulnerable populations. We travel abroad to Latin American countries such as Panama, Nicaragua, Peru, and the Dominican Republic to hold free medical clinics for underserved communities. We prepare the students who partake in our medical mission trips by hosting mock clinics, workshops, and orientations prior to their departure. Locally, we foster a sense of community through various events such as workshops, socials, and volunteer events. These opportunities allow members to also engage with and support local populations. GMT UCI creates the opportunity to acquire unique, hands-on experiences unlike any other volunteer work.

name: GoodSoil at UCI
description: The mission of GoodSoil at UCI is to provide a platform for Chinese-speaking students or English-speaking students who want to learn Chinese at UC Irvine to receive Christian faith based on Jesus's teachings in the Holy Bible.

name: Google Developer Group on Campus at UCI
description: Google Developer Group on Campus at UCI works to empower students of UC Irvine to connect, learn, and grow by fostering an inclusive developer community, bridging the gap between academic theory and industry practice, and creating opportunities for collaboration among students, faculty, industry professionals, and the broader Google developer ecosystem.

name: Goth Club at UCI
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide a place of community for students at UCI who are interested in, wish to become involved in, or learn about the goth subculture as well as other alternative subcultures.

name: Graduate and Family Housing
description: Student Housing strives to create student centered communities that promote academic success, safety and wellness, personal development and engagement.

name: Graduate Association of Biomedical Engineering Students-GABES
description: Graduate Association of Biomedical Engineering Students (GABES) at UC Irvine seeks to facilitate networking between students, industry, alumni, and the larger Orange County biomedical community. We aim to provide avenues that will allow graduate students to build experience in leadership and communications, skills essential for professional development.

name: Graduate Division
description: The UC Irvine Graduate Division mission is to serve as a catalyst for a world-class graduate educational experience, to foster oversight and communication of institutional academic policies, and to provide resources and essential services to promote the diversity and success of the next generation of leaders.Within the Graduate Division operates the Graduate & Postdoctoral Scholar Resource Center (GPSRC). The GPSRC is dedicated to supporting the academic and professional success of all UC Irvine graduate students and postdoctoral scholars. The GPSRC has everything you need to succeed! We offer certificate programs; writing support; funding opportunities; grant writing preparation; and workshops on various topics including communication, wellness, mentoring and much more! GPSRC events are open to current UCI graduate students and postdoctoral scholars. Guests (such as undergraduate students or alumni) may attend only if they have received prior approval from the event host and are registered in advance.About UC Irvine As one of the top doctorate-granting institutions in the United States, the University of California, Irvine fosters a collaborative and innovative research community. Our graduate students and postdoctoral scholars work with eminent faculty in highly-ranked programs, benefit from unparalleled support services, and get to experience everything that a great Southern California location has to offer.

name: GRADUATE MFA PROGRAM:ART
description: OverviewHeaded by an internationally distinguished faculty, the Graduate Program offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary environment for training in the visual arts.  The three-year MFA program comprises a series of core and elective classes in production, theory, and contemporary issues.  Graduate students may also take advantage of the academic excellence UCI provides as a leading research university by taking courses in other departments and programs.  Through a combination of faculty mentorship, seminars, and regular comprehensive peer critiques, the Department of Art affords an optimal intellectual setting for fostering creative and critical development.  In addition to faculty dedicated to facilitating students' understanding of visual art and its cultural contexts, graduate students have access to visiting artists through lectures, studio visits, and colloquia.

name: Graduate Program in Cognitive Sciences
description: Cognitive science is a multidisciplinary field integrating behavioral research, computational models, and neuroscience. UC Irvine provides the perfect modern environment for research training, as 1 of 62 universities in the U.S. and Canada elected to membership in the prestigious Association of American Universities, and the 9th best public university in the U.S. (U..S News & World Report, 2017).The Ph.D. degree programs prepare students for research and teaching careers in academia, industry, and government. The emphasis is on modern techniques of experimentation and theory construction. Special attention is given to providing hands-on research experience and equipping students with sophisticated mathematical and computing skills.

name: Graduate Public Health Association
description: The mission of Grad PHA is to cultivate a vibrant and inclusive community that enriches the graduate experience for public health students. We are dedicated to fostering a safe and engaging environment where diversity is celebrated, and every student feels valued and connected. Our commitment is to enhance the academic and social journey of our members through innovative activities and events that promote collaboration, well-being, and professional growth. By focusing on these pillars, Grad PHA aims to empower students to thrive both during their studies and in their future public health careers. We aspire to be a dynamic force that supports our students' immediate needs and contributes to their long-term success and the broader public health discourse.

name: Graduate Society of Women Engineers
description: The Graduate Society of Women Engineers is a branch of the Society of Women Engineers UCI Chapter and aims to support the women in engineering graduate student community through social, professional, and personal development events and opportunities.

name: Graduate Writing Hub
description: The Graduate Writing Hub - part of the Center for Excellence in Writing and Communication - provides support for graduate students and postdoctoral scholars' writing endeavors.

name: H1025
description: The purpose of the Organization is to provide a supportive and inclusive community for students to explore, practice, and grow in their Christian faith.

name: Haath A Cappella
description: Haath is the Indian Fusion A Cappella team at UCI, that was created with the vision of perfectly blending the intricate heritage of Indian music with the sounds of contemporary Western tunes. We believe that A Cappella is not just about creating and performing mixes using only our voices, but is also about the opportunity for us to appreciate all the diversity and complexity of the music that surrounds us. Through our unique combinations of different languages, musical styles, and beats, we hope to enchant audiences by showcasing the power of storytelling and music.

name: Hack at UCI
description: Hack at UCI is an organization that reclaims the word hack back to its original meaning, to solve a problem creatively and effectively. Hack at UCI aims to cultivate a community of technical students at the University of California, Irvine. While other clubs may focus on expressive or computational parts of technology, Hack at UCI aims to enhance the practical and professional skills for students that may benefit (e.g. majors from the School of ICS, School of Engineering, and much more). Hack at UCI hosts two Hackathons, ZotHacks, and IrvineHacks, similar to those hosted at other UCs, that encourage students to build amazing technical projects. With a plethora of open source tools, community resources and events, and technical workshops, there is ample opportunity for anyone to bring their technical and professional goals to reality.

name: Hansori
description: Hansori at UCI was formed in 2002 by four former students, who were inspired by Kim Duk Soo's Samulnori performance at the Barclay Theater. Since then, Hansori has been striving to spread Korean cultural awareness through the practice of traditional Korean drumming, known as Pungmul (풍물) and Samulnori (사물놀이). Hansori members learn and practice Korean percussion music that is performed by four traditional Korean instruments, representing four different weather components - thunder, rain, clouds, and wind. When played all together, they create “one sound”—the meaning of Hansori. Practices are held weekly throughout the school year to perform around Southern California with events including Lunar New Year celebrations, weddings, festivals, and many more.

name: Healing with Music at UCI
description: Our mission is to harness the power of music to promote joy, healing, and community engagement.We are primarily a music therapy and community health organization, providing college studentsof all majors, regardless of musical background, with avenues to engage with and promotemusic, whether through performing, assisting with events, or supporting outreach initiatives.

name: Health and Justice Advocates at UCI
description: As public health students at the University of California, Irvine, we believe that we have a responsibility to support and take action regarding public policy decisions that impact the health and wellbeing of everyone globally from all communities. We believe that everyone deserves to live, work, study, and play in a healthy environment, to have access to good quality and affordable healthcare, and to live free from discrimination regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, disability or ability, religious affiliation, immigration status, or gender identity. This student group will engage in political advocacy efforts such as contacting state and national government representatives, starting petitions, letter, call, or email campaigns and attending events such as town halls in order to advocate around key public health issues including:●	Discrimination against specific historically and contemporarily marginalized groups and its impact on health●	Mental health, student wellness, and pedagogical wellness●	Violence prevention, including firearms, injuries, and abuse among vulnerable populations●	Access to reproductive and sexual health care services●	Health and educational equity considerations from the COVID-19 pandemic●	Health consequences (physical and mental) among undocumented immigrants and their families due to discrimination, lack of access to health care, and (threats of) deportation.

name: Hearts for the Homeless at UC Irvine
description: Hearts for the Homeless is a student-led nonprofit organization that provides free blood-pressure screening opportunities and heart health education to homeless populations around the United States and globally. H4H International is a team of undergraduate students, medical students, Ph.D. students, medical doctors, and other professionals who are invested in improving the well-being of homeless communities around the world, soon including Irvine.

name: Help Unite the Middle East
description: HUME is an organization open for all students from schools such as UCLA and UCI. With a heart-centered on social responsibility, our mission revolves around enhancing the overall health and well-being of underserved communities located in the Middle East. As we believe in the power of unity and collaboration, we gather resources through our participating and local sponsors.

name: Her Campus
description: Her Campus, "A Collegiette's Guide to Life"  Description: Her Campus is an online magazine for college women that individualizes its content college-by-college by establishing My Campus branches at schools across the country. With national content on Style, Health, Love, DormLife, and Career, supplemented by campus-specific content produced by teams of students at 60+ colleges across the country, Her Campus serves as a hub for everything college women need to know about today.  Her Campus is written entirely by the nation's top college journalists. Since joining the Her Campus Team, our writers have been offered jobs and internships with the American Society of Magazine Editors (ASME) Intern Program and at Seventeen, Glamour, Teen Vogue, Marie Claire, InStyle, Harper\'s Bazaar, Hearst Digital Media Teen Network (Seventeen.com, CosmoGirl.com, DonateMyDress.org), O magazine, Reader\'s Digest, Details magazine, Us magazine, and Star magazine, among others.  Founded by three students while they were undergraduates at Harvard:  Stephanie Kaplan '10, Windsor Hanger '10, and Annie Wang '11.  Her Campus was a winner in Harvard College's business plan competition, the i3 Innovation Challenge, in March 2009. Since Her Campus's launch in September 2009, Her Campus has formed content partnerships with Seventeen magazine and The Huffington Post and formed marketing partnerships with brands including New Balance, Juicy Couture, Rent the Runway, and Lauren Merkin. The site has been featured on ABC News Now, Fox25 News, CNN Money, AOL Money College, and in The Boston Globe, U.S. News & World Report, seventeen.com, Business Insider, The Boston Herald, The Metro, YPulse.com, Jezebel.com, and The Chronicle of Higher Education, among others. In July 2010, Stephanie, Windsor, and Annie were named to Inc. magazine\'s 30 Under 30 Coolest Young Entrepreneurs.  HerCampus.com is the flagship website of Her Campus Media LLC. Her Campus Media LLC also owns HerCampusShop.com.  Our Mission:  - Define and provide a model for the future of online magazines by individualizing content - Fill the hole in the media marketplace for media that responds directly to the needs of college women - Serve as a career launching point for the nation\'s top college journalists by providing them with a national platform for the publication of their work - Connect companies with college students across the country in creative ways

name: HER Health Initiative
description: The HER Health Initiative at UCI is committed to advancing and protecting female reproductive rights, believing that access to comprehensive and equitable reproductive healthcare is essential for achieving gender equality. Our mission is to create a welcoming space where women can come together to learn, share, and advocate for their own rights and the rights of women in our nation. Through our efforts, we aim to empower women with the knowledge, support, and confidence needed to advocate for reproductive rights for themselves and others.Our organization focuses on raising awareness of the critical issues surrounding reproductive justice and healthcare access. By hosting educational events, partnering with advocacy groups, and working with healthcare professionals, HER Health Initiative provides resources and learning opportunities to help our members become informed advocates. We emphasize the importance of understanding the broader social, economic, and political challenges that impact women’s health, striving to inspire action and dialogue within our campus and community.HER Health Initiative envisions a world where reproductive health is viewed as a right, not a privilege. Through our collective efforts, we strive to inspire a new generation of advocates who are ready to support one another, challenge inequalities, and work toward a future in which all women feel safe, informed, and empowered to make choices about their health. Together, we are building a foundation of understanding, compassion, and advocacy for the rights and well-being of women everywhere.

name: Hermanas Unidas de UCI
description: The Mission of this organization is to provide graduate and professional resources and leadership opportunities for predominantly Chicana/Latina college students and alumni. We achieve this by participating/implementing community service events, networking events, retention and recruitment initiatives, and academic and professional development workshops and events.

name: Hiking Club at UCI
description: Hiking Club at UCI is a great opportunity to discover local trails alongside fellow UCI students with a common passion for hiking!We accept members of all skill levels. Hiking Club is more of an opportunity to make new friends and explore local trails!Socialize | Meet new peopleExercise | Avoid that freshman 15De-stress | Put aside stressful work

name: Hillel at UC Irvine
description: Hillel is an international organization throughout college campuses focused on fostering Jewish student involvment on campus. We provide a safe environment for students to join in fun activities and meet other Jewish students. Hillel welcomes all college students to come learn, teach, and experience different aspects of Judaism.

name: Hindu YUVA at UCI
description: The purpose of Hindu YUVA at UCI is to bring together both Hindu and non-Hindu students to raise awareness about what Hinduism is. As one of the largest and oldest religions in the world, we believe it is necessary that there be an organization on campus to represent the interests of the Hindu community present here. We hope to create a comfortable atmosphere where students can come and celebrate the Hindu culture. We hope to achieve our mission by having team-building games, yoga and meditation, lively and exciting debates, and presentations at our weekly meetings. In other words, we want to build a small Hindu community within UCI so that students can come and discover a home away from home.

name: Hmong Student Association
description: The Hmong Student Association at the University of California, Irvine is a revived student organization that strives to foster open communications between Hmong students, the Irvine community, and surrounding Hmong communities of Southern California. The organization strives to provide an atmosphere where students will be able to share and promote a deeper understanding of the Hmong culture towards one another and other students of the UCI community, promote higher education, and provide leadership and community service opportunities.

name: HoboBujo Club
description: HoboBujo Club strives to create a relaxed, inclusive, non-judgmental, and safe environment for students to express themselves creatively in journals, mainly through physical media such as pens, pencils, markers, and paper, emphasizing that there is no right or wrong way to be creative.

name: Hong Kong Student Union (HKSU)
description: Our mission at Hong Kong Student Union is to spread awareness of Hong Kong culture as well as to gather those who have interest in the culture. We are striving to expand our club by hosting cultural events which allow our students and club members to feel welcomed and included. The Hong Kong Student Union at UC Irvine targets our audience towards students who have a Hong Kong cultural background, however, we are open to anyone who has interest in learning more about our culture. Since Hong Kong is a relatively small place with a very unique culture, we hope to share this interesting culture with students at UC Irvine.We belong to U-852 organization which is made up of four UC schools to give more opportunities for our members and their members to share common cultures & interests.  Beside connecting activities and cooperation with U852, we also have long-term partnerships with other student associations in UCI. In the global perspective, HKSU@UCI has also joined University of Hong Kong Student Association (UHKSA), which has 14 others top university, fostering partnerships and cooperating with them and aiming to create an interschool community in both the U.S and Hong Kong region. We hope that everyone is able to meet new friends, learn new things, and enjoy a good time while they are with us in UC Irvine!

name: Hospice Care Association at UC Irvine
description: Our mission is to educate students on the importance of understanding end-of-life care by incorporating the advocacies of Hospice care. We empower students to serve and grow through compassion, empathy, and emotional resilience by fostering a connected community to further serve those who need it most. Through involvement with local Hospice organizations, opportunities for career exploration, and guidance on how to become a Hospice volunteer, we hope to promote medical bereavement support by exploring a differing side of healthcare.

name: Human Biology Club at UCI
description: The Human Biology Club at UCI aims to provide students with guidance towards a career in medicine with an emphasis on community outreach and involvement. We will participate in local volunteering events and clinical opportunities. We hope to connect members to each other, alumni, medical students, and health professionals. Additionally, our mentorship will provide our members with an understanding of how to achieve their academic goals. The Human Biology Club is not restricted to the major and welcomes anyone with an interest in human biology and medicine.

name: Human Resources Management Association at UCI
description: Our organization aims to educate young professionals on the nuances within the HR industry through guest speakers, mentorship and internship programs, professional workshops, and certification opportunities.

name: Ice Hockey Club at UCI
description: The Ice Hockey Club at UCI plays ice hockey on a recreational and a competitive level with the American Collegiate Hockey Association division 3 in the West Coast Hockey Conference tier 2. Our objectives is to build a network amongst people with similar interests, advancing social and communication skills, organizing and participating in competitions on a collegiate level, and improving Ice Hockey techniques through instruction and mentorship.

name: ICS Graduate Student Affairs
description: Join more than 800 graduate students studying virtually every area within the fields of Computer Science, Informatics, Networked Systems, Software Engineering and Statistics, as well as many new interdisciplinary topics. With more than 100 faculty members spanning three departments—Computer Science, Informatics and Statistics—this is a very exciting time to be a part of the Donald Bren School.

name: ICS Office of Outreach, Access & Inclusion
description: The Stacey Nicholas Office of Outreach, Access and Inclusion’s (OAI) mission is to recruit, retain, and graduate talented graduate and undergraduate students from historically excluded populations who are currently underrepresented in The Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences (ICS). https://oai.ics.uci.edu/#

name: ICS Student Council (ICSSC)
description: To improve student life of the Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences academically, socially, and professionally by creating and deepening the bonds between students, faculty, administration, companies, and alumni of the ICS School as well as similar groups outside of the Information and Computer Sciences.

name: If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice at UCI Law
description: If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice at UCI is a chapter of the national If/When/How organization whose mission is to train and mobilize law students and lawyers across the country to foster legal expertise and support for the realization of reproductive justice. We believe that individuals enjoy reproductive justice when they can each choose if, when, and how to create and sustain a family. Our chapter is focused on contributing to achieving this goal through sponsoring speaker panels on reproductive justice issues, getting students involved in lobbying and pro bono work, and continuing to fight for the preservation of reproductive rights in defiance of the Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.

name: Illuminations: The Chancellor's Arts & Culture Initiative
description: Building on UCI's demonstrated excellence in the creative arts and cultural programming, Illuminations aims to ensure that all of our students, regardless of major, have serious and meaningful exposure to the creative arts. In addition, we seek to strengthen the connections between UCI and our regional arts and culture centers and institutions.

name: IMED at UCI - FIMRC affiliated
description: Our name stands for "International Medicine, Education, and Development" and we are the chapter of a national organization at UC Irvine , the Foundation for the International Medical Relief of Children (FIMRC). Our mission is to increase medical care access and disease prevention for under-served and underprivileged children both locally and abroad.  IMED is a community service project organization which hosts a variety of events both locally and internationally. Our main current projects are: the Health Smart Project (health education in after school programs), the Orphanage Project (hosted primarily in Tijuana, Mexico), the Mentorship Project (healthcare physicians mentoring), the Outreach Project and the Global Actions Project (medical mission abroad). Health Smart allows our members to go to local after school programs to educate youth of various ages about staying healthy and proactive about their well-being. Orphanage Project works closely with an orphanage in Tijuana, Mexico where we spend a day with the children to teach them about health measures and science materials.
