We explore the cultural, ecological, and clinical aspects ofmycology with engaging presentations and outings for our members. Mushrooms have been ofhigh importance historically in many cultures all over the world. They are not often seen, butthey are incredibly abundant and play an important role in our forests. There are mushroomsthat can break down plastics, and many form symbiotic relationships with trees that promote athriving ecosystem. Fungi has been used to synthesize revolutionary pharmaceuticals, such aspenicillin. A wider understanding of fungi can fight the climate crisis and save lives. Through ourorganization, our members are exposed to research, activism, hobby, and career opportunitiesthey may not have known existed. We take our members on hikes to get hands-on experiencewith locating and identifying wild species. We also allow opportunities to attend larger eventswith professional speakers, like local mushroom fairs. With great results so far, we hope toencourage more students to spend time exploring the diverse world of mycology.

name: Na `Opio O Ka `Aina - Hawai'i Club at UCI
description: Na `Opio O Ka `Aina exists to ease the transition of students from Hawai'i and with the goal of spreading the Aloha spirit. Na `Opio o Ka `Aina (NOOK), which translates to "The Youth of the Land", was started in 1985 by several students from Hawai'i. The original purpose of NOOK was to ease the transition of Hawai'i students to the mainland lifestyle, as well as college life. Since these students are so far away from a culture so different from the one found in Irvine, it is often difficult for them to adjust to life on the mainland. Members share the Aloha spirit and spread customs from Hawai'i to the surrounding UCI community via cultural workshops, performances, and social events. As a club, we aim to create a community that allows students from Hawai'i to feel at home on the mainland while sharing the Aloha spirit and culture from Hawai'i with as many people as possible.

name: National Disabled Law Student Association
description: National Disabled Law Student Association (NDLSA) at UCI Law aims to eliminate the stigma of disability within the legal profession, provide support for law students and prospective law students, and foster an inclusive and accessible environment for law students.NDLSA at UCI Law asserts that the ideal way to make UCI Law accessible for students is to enact widespread non-exclusionary change that benefits the entire community. However, NDLSA at UCI Law acknowledges that in cases where this is not possible, it is still important to advocate for each student getting their needs met in an individualized manner.

name: National Lawyers Guild at UCI - NLG
description: The University of California, Irvine, School of Law ("UCI Law") Chapter of the National Lawyers Guild ("NLG") is an association dedicated to the support and defense of economic and social justice, and to progressive change rather than the acceptance of the status quo. We seek to educate ourselves and the community about issues affecting economic and social justice, to provide law students with pro bono opportunities in support of these goals, and to increase awareness of the UCI community on issues surrounding economic and social justice. We seek to unite the lawyers, law students, legal workers and jailhouse lawyers of America in an organization which shall function as an effective political and social force in the service of the people, to the end that economic and social justice are basic human rights and must be protected and expanded.

name: National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE)
description: Our mission is to increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically succeed professionally and positively impact the community.

name: National Society of Leadership and Success [The]
description: The National Society of Leadership and Success is an organization that assists people in discovering and achieving their goals. Members will learn how to achieve their goals through the Society's leadership speaker series as well as through being part of a community where like minded success-oriented individuals come together and help one another. In addition, not only will the members succeed in their own lives, but they will also create a better world through community service and cooperation.   The core philosophy of the society is for our members to achieve their dreams with meaningful support and dedicated action.

name: National Student Speech Language Hearing Association Chapter at UCI - NSSLHA
description: Our mission is to bridge the gap created by the absence of a dedicated Communication Science and Disorders (CSD) program at UCI, fostering professional interest and providing essential resources to students pursuing research or clinical careers in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology.

name: Native American Law Students Association
description: The mission of the Native American Law Students Association is to gather Indigenous students and allies to create community; discuss Indigenous socio-legal issues and ongoing affairs; emphasize the study of tribal and federal Indian law and the effect of law on Indigenous communities; promote Indigenous wellness; recruit Indigenous students and faculty; and provide volunteer and service opportunities in support of Indigenous communities.Indigenous refers to any of the original peoples of North America, South America, and Oceania. We emphatically disavow the use of blood quantum, which is a tool of genocide, as a measure of indigeneity, instead emphasizing community, family, and tribal affiliation, and values. NALSA is open to Indigenous students and allies.NALSA is a pending chapter of the National Native American Law Students Association.

name: Navigators
description: To advance the gospel of Jesus and His kingdom into the nations through spiritual generations of laborers living and discipling among the lost.

name: Neonatal Nursing Club
description: The Neonatal Nursing Club (NNC) is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing education, advocacy, and professional development in neonatal nursing. The club provides opportunities for UCI health students to gain hands-on experience, mentorship, and networking with healthcare professionals, particularly in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).The organization emphasizes evidence-based practice, family-centered care, and the integration of classroom knowledge with real-world clinical experiences. NNC aims to empower and support health students to excel academically, achieve their health-related educational goals, and prepare for successful careers in neonatal and pediatric nursing.By creating a safe, inclusive space for collaboration, discussion, and skill development, the club fosters leadership, career readiness, and lifelong learning. Through events, workshops, and community engagement, NNC also raises awareness about ongoing challenges in maternal and infant health, including disparities that impact diverse populations. The club seeks to inspire the next generation of neonatal nurses to deliver high-quality, compassionate care, while providing opportunities for personal growth, professional networking, and academic excellence.

name: New Forum
description: New Forum is a publication dedicated to UC Irvine's undergraduate creative writing. We take submissions of short fiction, poetry, and original artwork every quarter, and selected submissions will be printed in our quarterly publication. At New Forum, we look for compelling storytelling and language that unzips and makes us see again.

name: New Life Fellowship
description: We are a Christian organization serving Chinese-speaking students enrolled at UC Irvine. We aim to help students know Jesus Christ and His Gospel.

name: New Swan Shakespeare Center
description: The New Shakespeare Center at the University of California, Irvine aims to share the drama of Shakespeare and his contemporaries with the campus and community. An interschool initiative between the School of Humanities and the Claire Trevor School of the Arts, New Swan Shakespeare presents lectures, reading groups, workshops, symposia, mock trials, and performances, all designed to educate and delight enthusiasts of the Bard from all walks of life, including students, staff, teachers, scholars, lifelong learners, and families. UCI is the only campus in the UC system that is home to an annual summer Shakespeare festival supported by a varied menu of academic programming. Many prominent scholars and artists contribute to Shakespearean research, teaching, and performance at UCI. Our distinctive programming advances scholarship, promotes group learning, and encourages engagement with the First Folio and other library holdings.

name: New Venture Competition
description: Calling All Creators, Inventors, and Aspiring Entrepreneurs! The UCI New Venture Competition offers you the opportunity to form a team, launch a startup and potentially fund a business idea – all within seven months. The competition is open to all UCI students, staff members and researchers as well as community members. Teams compete for $100,000 in cash prizes plus additional professional services!Competitors have full control and ownership over what their team creates. We connect you with potential teammates, provide you with the tools to transform your idea into a concept, and even match teams with industry mentors to help you develop your concept into a viable business.Please register for the workshops that you would like to attend. Those who have registered will be sent access links to Zoom workshop sessions and live Q&A sessions.

name: ANTrepreneur Center
description: Whether a UCI Student is just curious to experience the process of entrepreneurship, have a idea burning inside them, or have already formed a company, the ANTrepreneur Center's mission is to provide a safe place where they can start. Book a meeting with us today : https://cglink.me/2eo/m1377

name: Wayfinder Incubator
description: Wayfinder is a highly structured incubator, through UCI Beall Applied Innovation, that connects UC-affiliated startups with essential resources needed to launch, grow and succeed.Housed inside the Cove @ UCI, our collaborative team of business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors and technology transfer experts eat, sleep and drink innovation. Using our combined experience, we help fine-tune a strategic process that leads innovation with both commercial promise and the potential to meet real needs, from formation to funding.

name: Innovation Advisors
description: The Innovation Advisor network is a group of local business leaders who volunteer their time to support the development of the UCI Beall Applied Innovation entrepreneurial ecosystem. The goals of the Innovation Advisor network are to increase the likelihood of success of UCI-affiliated ventures by providing insightful and actionable guidance and mentorship to individuals and teams and to foster engagement between the University and the local entrepreneurial community to accelerate the commercialization of University innovations.

name: Newkirk Center for Science & Society
description: The Newkirk Center focuses on the interaction between science and society, including the role of society in the production of scientific knowledge and technological systems and artifacts and the effects of scientific knowledge on society.  It seeks to explore and think critically about the process by which scientific information is communicated to the public and policy-makers.  It fosters the use of science to enhance the environment, education, health care, public infrastructure, and justice. The Center carries out its mission through support of research, public engagement, and events.

name: Next Generation of Ingenuity
description: In partnership with UCI Beall Applied Innovation, the ANTrepreneur Center started Next Generation of Ingenuity (NGI) as a supportive community of students who are class leaders in the representation and advocation of entrepreneurship at UC Irvine. The NGI Ambassadors help the Antrepreneur Center grow our outreach to the different Schools and clubs within UCI and around the larger community. Entrepreneurship experience is not necessary to apply!

name: Nigerian Student Association
description: The Nigerian Student Association at the University of California, Irvine is firmly committed to uniting and strengthening the Nigerian and greater African community at UCI for the purposes of networking, cultural enrichment, open dialogue, and civic engagement.

name: Nihon Karate Club at UCI
description: The Nihon Karate Club at UCI is a beginner-friendly club that pursues both the recreational and competitive aspects of the Japanese martial art of Karate. We strive for mental and physical self-improvement as we develop self-defense skills, continue Japanese Karate culture traditions, and cultivate a strong Karate community. We are also a competitive sports club associated with the World Karate Federation and Japanese Karate-Do Jinen Kai.Whether you have some experience or none at all, we welcome you to join our club! Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have questions.

name: No Voice Alone Acapella - NOVA Acapella
description: NOVA is a diverse, all-gender a cappella group at the University of California, Irvine. We are dedicated to helping each member grow as a vocalist and performer through guidance, collaboration, and creativity.

name: NORD Students for Rare Chapter at UC Irvine
description: The mission of NORD Students for Rare Chapters is to increase awareness about treatments and care for patients with rare and chronic disorders. Further we aim to allow students the opportunity to network with professionals in the field rare disease research and care to push the boundaries of knowledge in the field of rare disorders while we provide them with more knowledge about how to pursuit a career in healthcare and its requirements.

name: Nu Alpha Kappa Fraternity, Inc.
description: Nu Alpha Kappa Fraternity, Inc. Psi Chapter at UC Irvine was established on August 18, 2012. We're a Latino-based fraternity that encompasses and values all cultures. We pride ourselves in our three pillars of Academic Excellence, Culture, Brotherhood. Through these pillars, we pride ourselves in being "Men of Mind...Men of Culture...Men of Pride." It is also through these pillars that we aim to improve our campus and surrounding communities with events that will empower our academic endeavors as well as inspiring gentlemen from all backgrounds to seek leadership, community service, and academic-success.

name: Nu Rho Psi at UCI
description: Nu Rho Psi at UCI is a chapter of the Nu Rho Psi National Honor Society. Our mission is to develop the next generation of neuroscientists and shape their career trajectories by providing immersive research, training, community outreach, and professional development experiences.

name: Nuestra Grad
description: The Nuestra Grad committee is in charge of the annual NUESTRA GRADUATION. This is an annual event for Chicana/o Latinx students who wish to participate in a more intimate celebration in addition to the regular UCI commencement ceremonies. The event is a bilingual and bi-cultural celebration that is open to all students and UCI community that honors Latinx students personal success and academic achievement in higher education. The program allows graduates to recognize their family, friends, and others who have provided support and encouragement during their college years.

name: Nursing Science Student Association at UCI
description: Our mission is to provide resources, opportunities, and a network that enhances the educational experience and professional development of our members.

name: Ocean Club at UCI
description: The primary purpose of the Ocean Club is to foster a community of individuals who share a passion for exploring and learning about the ocean and its surrounding environments, such as beaches, tide pools, and marine ecosystems. This club serves as a platform for students to connect, engage in ocean-related activities, and promote marine conservation awareness.

name: Office of Academic Integrity and Student Conduct
description: The Office of Academic Integrity & Student Conduct is responsible for ensuring that students comply with and understand university policies related to academic integrity and student conduct by promoting student learning and development.

name: Office of Campus Organizations & Volunteer Programs
description: The Office of Campus Organizations provides opportunities for students to pursue personal and professional goals through involvement with Registered Campus Organizations. We promote leadership development by providing resources, innovative programming, and advising for Campus Organizations and the campus community. We aspire to provide transformative leadership experiences that foster a community of engagement and campus spirit.Volunteer Programs provides opportunities for community engagement and leadership development. Through mutually beneficial campus and community partnerships, students explore social issues by engaging in direct service, reflection, and critical dialogue. We aspire to be a resource that encourages and empowers the campus community to become global leaders.

name: Office of Campus Social Work
description: The Office of Campus Social Work supports UCI students during situations and crises that may be impacting their personal and academic well-being, through short-term resource referral and long-term case management. Services are available to the entire UCI community at no cost, by appointment only.

name: Office of Civic Engagement
description: The Office of Civic Engagement provides students with opportunities to engage as citizens and community members in a variety of curricular and co-curricular activities that enhance their education and professional development. Part of the Division of Undergraduate Education, the Office includes the Civic and Community Engagement minor, the UCDC Internship Program, and UCCS Sacramento Internship Program.

name: Office of Inclusive Excellence
description: OIE provides campus resources, mounts training and education, conducts responsive research, and builds and sustains partnerships with universities and colleges that share this commitment.

name: Office of Information Technology
description: The Office of Information Technology (OIT) is responsible for supporting the IT needs of UC Irvine faculty, students, and staff.  Our mission is to provide information technology leadership, services, and innovative solutions to promote the research, education and community service goals of the University.

name: Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning (OVPTL)
description: The Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning (OVPTL) promotes students' academic and future success through campus and community partnerships.  The Office oversees 3 divisions that provide services to the campus community to fulfill this mission – Division of Undergraduate Education, Division of Teaching Excellence and Innovation, and Division of Summer Session.

name: Division of Teaching Excellence and Innovation (DTEI)
description: The Division of Teaching Excellence and Innovation (DTEI) is dedicated to partnering with faculty, graduate students, and postdocs to maximize students' academic success. We accomplish this by cultivating exceptional learning environments across campus through pedagogical development opportunities focused on integrating innovative, evidence-based teaching practices. DTEI's goals align with the Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning (OVPTL) and Pillar 2 and 4 of the UCI Strategic Plan:1. Enhance pedagogical training for faculty, graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff by providing and developing certification, teaching assistant training, and fellowship programs.2. Partner with campus researchers to collect and disseminate data on evidence-based practices that the campus community can use to improve student success.3. Promote the effective utilization of digital technologies by the UCI community to foster teaching innovation and enhance student face-to-face and online learning.    4. Coordinate efforts to systematically align campus learning environments with current and emerging educational practices to maximize student success.5. Evaluate the impact of DTEI programs and campus learning environments on both students and instructors, utilizing assessment data to further improve teaching and learning on campus.

name: Division of Undergraduate Education (DUE)
description: DUE provides leadership, advocacy and coordination for campus initiatives that impact undergraduate education and enhance student access and retention. Working with faculty, the Academic Senate, academic support staff and others, DUE units deliver a wide variety of academic programs and services that support undergraduate teaching and learning campuswide.

name: Older Wiser Law Students
description: The purpose of this organization is to foster a supportive and thriving community for students who have taken time off prior to law school, are transitioning into second careers, have previously pursued an advanced degree, have families, are parents, and others who view their academic path as non-traditional.

name: Open Jam
description: Open Jam is a community that aims to create music performance, collaboration, and appreciation opportunities for students at UCI. We not only foster a community within our club, but contribute to the schoolwide community through coordinating events and performances with other groups. We welcome members of any and all skill levels, and encourage the development of musical skills through events such as open mic nights and group lessons-- All that is required to join Open Jam is a desire to appreciate and play music! Check our Facebook page for more information and time and meeting locations, or our Instagram or Youtube channel to see videos of club members' performances.

name: Optical Computing Club at UCI
description: The mission of “OCC@UCI” is to cultivate interest in optical and photonic computing and to developan interdisciplinary community at UCI centered on light-based information processing.The club is dedicated to provide a platform for engagement in discussion and empoweringstudents with the skills to design, simulate, and implement computational systems that leverageoptics. By centering the club around a Journal Club, members will critically discuss and analyzescholarly work related to optical computing architectures and photonic information systems. Tosupplement these discussions, the club hosts educational seminars introducing foundational andadvanced concepts from optics, machine learning, and engineering, as well as project-based workshops designed to reinforce and apply the material covered.

name: Orange County Chapter of the Association of Environmental Professionals at UCI (OCAEP)
description: The Association of Environmental Professionals (AEP) is a non-profit organization established to facilitate greater relationships between professionals and students interested in environmental related jobs and to foster the mutual professional growth of our members through those relationships.

name: Order of Omega
description: Order of Omega is a leadership honor society for members of Greek organizations.  Order of Omega recognizes juniors and seniors who have exemplified high standards in the areas of scholarship, leadership, involvement within their respective organization and within the Greek, campus, and local community. Members are selected from the top 3% of students at each institution. To date, over 500 chapters have been chartered throughout North America, each sharing the common goal of recognizing the many outstanding student leaders at their institution.

name: Ordinary College South Orange County at UCI
description: The mission of Ordinary College South Orange County is to help students find a community that will prioritize their spiritual lives and the kingdom of God by studying the Gospel and spending time to fellowship with one another.

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: OCF transforms the lives of college students by guiding them along the path to Jesus Christ through His Church, cultivating a campus community of worship, witness, service, fellowship, and education.

name: osu! at UCI
description: osu! at UCI is a community made for individuals interested in osu!, a free, multiplayer rhythm game.

name: OutLaw at UCI Law
description: OutLaw at UCI Law facilitates civic and social activities by and for the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, and asexual (LGBTQIA+) community at UCI Law through education, community empowerment, and activism.   Education and Scholarship: OutLaw at UCI Law promotes discussions about the intersections of sexual orientation, gender identity, race, ethnicity, and the law. LGBTQIA+ communities experience unique challenges to attaining access to justice and inclusion in the legal industry. Many LGBTQIA+ clients lack access to competent representation. They face unfriendly legal precedent, attacks from legislatures, and disparate enforcement. We seek to highlight local and national conversations about these issues and to provide opportunities for related scholarship at UCI Law. Recently, OutLaw was awarded funding for a multi-day symposium on legal issues that affect transgender communities.  Community Empowerment: OutLaw provides networking, social, and leadership opportunities for LGBTQIA+ students, faculty, staff, and alumni. We support and empower each other to become stronger advocates and legal professionals by holding space for LGBTQIA+ members of the UCI Law community. Please contact receive updates about upcoming events.  Activism: OutLaw connects UCI Law community members with opportunities to advocate for the safety, inclusion, and equality of people of all sexual orientations and gender identities. We encourage all OutLaw members to participate in pro bono projects that serve local LGBTQIA+ communities, such as the Transgender Legal Assistance Clinic at the LGBT Center OC in Santa Ana.  Become a Member: All currently enrolled J.D. and LLM students at UCI Law are eligible to be members, including joint degree program participants, faculty, and staff.

name: Pakistani Student Association
description: The Pakistani Student Association is an on-campus cultural club dedicated to expressing our heritage, educating Pakistanis and Non-Pakistanis alike, and creating a social atmosphere to make lifelong friends in. With the help of our Board and club members, we have a history of throwing spectacular culture shows, successful fundraisers, and have shown just how rich our culture truly is. This year we strive to take that one step further and keep our community involved as much as possible, because in the end, we must keep our culture alive.

name: Palo Verde Housing Community
description: Student Housing strives to create student centered communities that promote academic success, safety and wellness, personal development and engagement.

name: Panhellenic Association at UCI
description: The Panhellenic Association serves as the collegiate governing body of the 7 National Panhellenic Conference sororities on the UC Irvine campus.  The Panhellenic Council is composed of 12 executive board officers. The Panhellenic Association works to unite sorority women on common goals, create a network of support for chapters and members, and serve our SFL and University community. We sponsor interactive programs and activities not only for sorority women, but for all students, such as educational speakers, scholarship programs, and quarterly Risk Events.

name: Pariyan Punjab Diyan
description: To establish a cultural initiative centered around Giddha, a traditional folk dance form originating from the Punjab region, we aim to create an inclusive platform for our community at UC Irvine. While traditionally performed by women, we welcome all interested participants to join us in celebrating this vibrant and expressive art form. Driven by the absence of a Giddha team at UC Irvine, we seek to fill this gap and provide a space for individuals from diverse backgrounds to come together and experience the joy of Giddha. This initiative is not just about preserving cultural heritage but also about fostering unity, expression, and storytelling through dance and music. Giddha offers a unique opportunity for participants to connect with their cultural roots, express emotions, and build strong bonds of friendship and camaraderie. By opening this initiative to all, we hope to promote diversity, inclusivity, and cross-cultural understanding within our campus community. Through workshops, performances, and collaborative events, we invite everyone to join us in exploring the beauty and significance of Giddha.

name: Patient Navigation Network at UCI
description: The purpose of Patient Navigation Network at UCI is to reduce barriers to healthcare access and improve continuity of care in partnership with local clinics, senior residences, hospices, and community organizations by providing structured, non-clinical patient navigation and practical patient education.

name: Peer Academic Advising Program
description: The Peer Academic Advising Program provides valuable services for all UCI undergraduate students. It is the source of student-to-student academic counseling based not only on academic, but also personal experiences of UCI students. In addition, we work closely with other offices on campus that provide services for students and participate in many programs for prospective applicants to UCI.Peer Academic Advisors are juniors and seniors from every academic unit and division on campus. Before beginning work in our respective advising offices, we undergo a rigorous quarter long training followed by continued bi-monthly training throughout the academic year, which covers issues related to: UCI policies and procedures, academic counseling, campus resources, and more. PAAs come from a wide range of ethnic, religious, scholastic, and extracurricular backgrounds. When you come in for an advising session, you can rest assured knowing that you are in the hands of UCI's most knowledgeable and involved students. Never be afraid to ask us for information–  you will be surprised at how much we know!

name: Pharmaceutical Sciences Mentorship Program
description: The Pharmaceutical Sciences Mentorship Program (PSMP) is designed to help incoming students ease the transition from high school or college to a university. This program provides students with the opportunity to be paired with a current Pharm Sci student to learn more about UCI and the Pharm Sci major. Incoming students will not only get the chance to gain deeper insight about the campus, its resources, programs, and major, but they will also create friendships with their mentor and other mentees. In addition, mentors and mentees will participate in various socials throughout the academic year in order to help build connections with peers and other Pharmaceutical Sciences programs.

name: Pharmaceutical Sciences Student Council
description: The mission of PSC is to foster a community within undergraduate Pharmaceutical Science majors through student advocacy, establishing professional relationships, and providing career related opportunities for the development of our future professions as part of a greater effort to help students achieve greater academic success.

name: PhD Program in Visual Studies
description: The PhD program in Visual Studies draws from a number of disciplines to explore the meanings, practices, and processes of looking and imaging across historical periods and diverse cultures. Visual Studies is inclusive and broad-ranging in its methods and approaches as well as its objects of inquiry, which include African American and African Diasporic visual cultures; the art and archeology of the ancient and medieval Persian/Iranian worlds including Islamic Central and South Asia; Asian and Asian American art, photography, and cinema; Latin American and Latino/a/x visual cultures; contemporary art and exhibition histories; and film, television, and digital media.UCI offers one of the premier graduate programs in Visual Studies, with core faculty drawn from the departments of Art History and Film & Media Studies. Our particular theoretical strengths include archaeological, architectural and environmental theory, cultural studies, critical race theory, feminist and queer studies, museum studies, postcolonial theory, and digital technologies. In addition, our graduate students may choose to supplement their Visual Studies degrees with interdisciplinary graduate certificates in Ancient Iran and the Premodern Persianate World, Asian American Studies, Chicano/Latino Studies, Critical Theory, Feminist Studies, or Latin American Studies, among others. Visual Studies is also proud to be one of the founding members of the School of the Humanities' Black Studies Cluster, which offers additional programmatic and funding support for VS students working in this area.Our location near Los Angeles gives students access to the rich cultural offerings and research institutions of southern California, such as the Getty Center and Getty Villa, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the ONE National Gay and Lesbian Archives, the Los Angeles Museum of Natural History, Los Angeles County Museum of Art, San Diego Museum of Art, UCLA's Film & Television Archive, and the Huntington Library, among other institutions. We admit all students, with BAs or MAs, directly into the PhD program in small cohorts with multi-year funding packages. We encourage prospective students to review our faculty profiles and contact the faculty members who work in their potential areas of interest before applying to learn more about their teaching and advising.The annual admissions deadline is December 1.

name: Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity
description: Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity, International is a professional law fraternity advancing integrity, compassion and courage through service to the student, the school, the profession and the community.

name: Phi Beta Delta at UCI
description: Phi Beta Delta at the University of California, Irvine is dedicated to recognizing and promoting academic excellence, leadership, and cross-cultural understanding within the Hispanic and international communities. Our mission is to empower scholars of Hispanic heritage and those committed to global engagement through scholarship, service, and cultural exchange. We strive to create a supportive community that celebrates diversity and prepares members to lead with compassion and commitment to positive change in an interconnected world. Through our collaboration with the Spanish Department and their faculty and graduate students, we aim to create opportunities for all interested in better understanding and celebrating our individuality.

name: Phi Chi Pre-Health Honor Society
description: To provide a forum wherein Physicians and Students of medicine may cometogether, to their mutual benefit, in a brotherhood seeking the development ofthe higher qualities of medicine; of nobler impulses of heart; of more profoundscholastic achievement; of devotion to the art and science of medicine; and of acommunion of kindred hearts pledged to support each other in times of joy, aswell as adversity.

name: Phi Chi Theta
description: To promote the cause of higher business education and training for all individuals, to foster high ideals for everyone pursuing a career in business; to encourage fraternity and cooperation among people preparing for such careers; and to stimulate the spirit of sacrifice and unselfish devotion to the attainment of such ends

name: Phi Delta Epsilon Medical Fraternity - CA Epsilon
description: Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a lifelong commitment to our guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education through fellowship, service, mentoring, and formal training in leadership, science, and ethics.  Our organization is the only professional fraternity on campus to provide singular, specialized help to all pre-medical students. We promote a familial environment to assist them on the rigorous path to medical school along with holding philanthropic and educational events throughout the year to showcase our excellence. We offer everyone the opportunity to be a part of the larger international organization that spans the entire nation to help build a grand network by the time they graduate and apply.

name: Phi Gamma Delta
description: Phi Gamma Delta exists to promote lifelong friendships, to reaffirm high ethical standards and values, and to foster personal development in the pursuit of excellence. Phi Gamma Delta is committed to providing opportunities to each brother to develop responsibility, leadership, scholarship, and social skills in order to become a fully contributing member of society.

name: Phi Kappa Psi
description: The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity is committed to bettering individuals in order to improve society. To that end, we strive to provide undergraduate members with the opportunity to get as much out of their campus experience as possible, while working within their chapters to effect change in their communities. Over 70,000 alumni provide a foundation of support for our undergraduates and are able to band together as Phi Psis through Alumni Associations across the nation.  Mission  The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity is an association of men of integrity who strive to develop the individual in his intellect, in his involvement in the community, and in his faith. Recognizing and valuing the diversity of all, the Fraternity unites the principals and traditions of our past with the resources and creativity of our present to provide an environment in which our members can realize their highest potential. To this end, we offer a lifelong experience, guided by our faith in a power greater than ourselves, in contributing to the betterment of both the individual and the community.

name: Phi Lambda Rho Sorority, Inc.
description: The purpose of Phi Lambda Rho Sorority, Inc. is to provide a lifelong sisterhood based on facilitating the advancement of women of color through higher education. Our mission is to give back to our community, especially our marginalized youth while celebrating and promoting the Chicana/Latina culture.

name: Photonics @ UCI
description: Photonics @ UCI is the local student chapter for the Optical Society of America (OPTICA) and Society for Optics and Photonics (SPIE).

name: Physician Assistants Coming Together at UCI - PACT
description: Our mission is to help educate and prepare students for the physician assistant profession. We strive to assist members in gaining more knowledge about the profession, application process, and various healthcare experiences. In addition to our networking opportunities, we host workshops, community service events, fundraisers, and socials to create a supportive environment for pre-PA students.

name: Physics Graduate Caucus
description: The Physics Grad Caucus seeks to enhance the physics graduate student experience in three primary ways: To provide a voice for physics graduate students in departmental affairs. To facilitate scientific and social interaction between physics graduate students of all different subfields. To provide physics graduate students a forum beyond official department channels to improve their education, research, and prospects for postgraduate work.

name: Pi Beta Phi (Pi Phi)
description: The mission of Pi Beta Phi Fraternity for women is to promote friendship, develop women of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service.

name: Pi Kappa Alpha
description: Pi Kappa Alpha is dedicated to developing men of integrity, intellect, and high moral character and to fostering a truly lifelong fraternal experience.

name: Pickleball at UCI
description: This organization’s mission is to create a welcoming, social environment for the UCI community to enjoy pickleball as a sport through recreational and competitive play.

name: Pilipinx Pre-Health Undergraduate Student Organization (PUSO)
description: Pilipinx Pre-Health Undergraduate Student Organization (PUSO) is a social and academic organization with the following goals: 1. To provide service, guidance, and support to pre-health students. 2. To sponsor programs for minority youth to encourage their entrance into health professions. 3. To increase the number of culturally sensitive health care professionals. 4. To serve the campus and the community of Irvine as well as the Pilipino community at large. 5. To spread "PUSO Love."

name: Pilipinx-Americans in Social Studies - PASS
description: Pilipinx-Americans in Social Studies (PASS) is an organization that focuses on fields relating to business, law, humanities, social sciences, and social ecology. PASS is a “community within a community” striving to increase the representation of Pilipinxs/Filipinxs and other minorities within professional industries while providing a social support network that promotes academic excellence, career development, community involvement, and leadership opportunities for students in the UCI (University of California, Irvine) and Pilipinx/Filipinx communities.

name: Planned Parenthood Generation Action
description: Planned Parenthood Generation Action at the University of California, Irvine (hereinafter referred to as PPGA at UCI) exists to educate the university community about reproductive health and rights, to translate increased awareness into pro-choice activism on campus, and to serve as a coalition partner to state, national, and international reproductive rights efforts.PPGA at UCI believes in the fundamental right of every individual to manage their fertility. PPGA at UCI supports full access to comprehensive reproductive and complementary health care services in settings that preserve and protect the essential privacy and rights of each individual; advocates for public policies that guarantee these rights and ensure access to such services; and supports access to medically accurate educational programs that enhance understanding of human sexuality.PPGA at UCI extends its activism not only to reproductive rights but to reproductive justice, as defined by Sister Song as the human right to maintain personal bodily autonomy, have children, not have children, and parent the children we have in safe and sustainable communities.PPGA at UCI intends to destigmatize sex, sexuality, and reproductive health by increasing health literacy and awareness to the campus community about available services, resources, and general education.

name: Platypus at UCI
description: The Platypus Affiliated Society, established in December 2006, organizes reading groups, public fora, research and journalism focused on the problems and tasks inherited from the "Old" (1920s–30s), "New" (1960s–70s) and post-political (1980s–90s) Left for the possibilities of emancipatory politics today.

name: Poker Strategy Club
description: The Poker Strategy Club provides a learning environment where students can study and practice poker as a strategic game. Our mission is to teach both foundational and modern poker concepts—from game theory optimal (GTO) play and pot odds to adaptive strategies such as exploitative play—while exploring decision-making, probability, and psychology in a fun, social, and no-stakes setting.

name: Politics, Unity, Noize, and Knowledge club
description: The P.U.N.K Club was formed in a time where public injustice was on the rise and community service was at an all time low. Our club is made to educate and empower the youth about current situations that affect different sectors of the world to cause a positive change. We aim to encourage a new generation's leaders, uplift empathy, and increase meaningful volunteer hours.

name: Powerlifting Club at UCI
description: Powerlifting Club at UCI was founded by Rainee Khabagnote and EJ Torralba in 2014. The Club has grown to become a well-known and respected Collegiate Powerlifting Team. We are both a competitive and recreational team with many members holding American and State records. Our members primarily compete in the USAPL; however, some compete in the USPA.  Our focus is assisting every member in reaching their full potential as both an individual and also as part of something bigger than themselves.  Important Facts: - All members must register with UCI Club Sports and pay the $15 fee - There will be optional meetings/practices TBD

name: Pre-Dental Society at UC Irvine - PDS
description: The Pre-Dental Society at UC Irvine is dedicated to helping students on their journey in pursuing a career in dentistry. We strive to create the best environment for pre-dental students through meetings with Dental School Representatives, workshops, field trips, presentations, community service and social events. We provide opportunities for students to gain valuable knowledge and insight into dentistry in an environment where students are able to network with one another and build friendships. Our members are given opportunities to strengthen their application for dental school through building their leadership skills in an altruistic environment.

name: Pre-Health Alliance
description: Spreading awareness to the community as a pre-health organization working with all fields of medicine while educating our members on the available careers of healthcare to pursue. Here we aim to network amongst various influential organizations in hopes of educating and inspiring the general public and future health care professionals. We promote an interdisciplinary approach by working with all aspects of healthcare through community outreach, as well as clinical environments, while fostering network opportunities with healthcare professionals.

name: Pre-Health Club at UCI
description: Our mission as the Pre-Health Club at UCI is to inspire and empower pre-health students by providing a comprehensive education, supportive mentorship, and motivational resources to guide students on their pre-health journeys. We are dedicated to fostering a collaborative environment that builds a community that fosters growth, resilience, and encouragement that leads to the success of students’ careers as pre-health students. Through engaging events, thoughtful speakers, and various health-related opportunities offered, we aim to prepare our members to become competent healthcare workers and make meaningful contributions to the health and well-being of others.

name: Pre-Law Latinx Association
description: As the Pre-Law Latinx Association at the University of California, Irvine, we believe in increasing Latinx matriculation in post-grad avenues alongside law programs that serve to increase educational attainment within the Latinx community. We strive to develop a network of social support with resources easily available to students in the forms of mentorship, LSAT preparation, law school program preparedness, personal statement workshops, guest speakers involved in the legal field, and skill-development to enhance students' preparedness to succeed in law school.  We hope to establish an ever-growing Latinx-based club at UCI that will strive to create a welcoming community for all marginalized students, predominantly identifying of Latinx descent, seeking to attend law school and/or pursue in the legal fields.

name: Pre-Law Society at UC Irvine
description: Pre-Law Society at UC Irvine is dedicated to assisting UC Irvine undergraduates who are looking to pursue a career in law or legal studies. Our organization strives to provide UC Irvine undergraduates with tools needed to be successful in law schools such as opportunities to see lawyers on the job, create connections, develop leadership skills and more hands-on experiences in the field of law. Pre-Law Society hosts diverse programs (e.g., LSAT informational seminars, law school admissions panel, as well as speaker panels) to help UCI undergraduates reach an informed decision about their career.

name: Pre-Occupational Therapy Student Society
description: To create and support fellow UCI students who are interested in Occupational Therapy, while also providing them with the resources and opportunities they may need towards their path to becoming a successful therapist.

name: Pre-Pharmacy Society (PPS) at UC Irvine
description: A campus organization based on student leadership and team building, Pre-Pharmacy Society (PPS) at UCI is dedicated to providing a social environment that encourages students interested in pharmacy to thrive as competitive applicants and as student leaders. We offer the tools necessary to approach the field with confidence through presented information (i.e. general insight, academia requirements, healthcare industry, etc.) and hands-on experience (i.e. volunteer, internship, jobs, etc.). By utilizing guest speaker, pharmacy school trips, community service events, and networking opportunities, PPS at UCI engages the aptitude of students to help them decide whether or not to pursue the field of pharmacy.

name: Pre-Veterinary and Animal Wellness Association (PAWA)
description: The Pre-Veterinary and Animal Wellness Association (PAWA) is dedicated to helping animals and supporting students exploring careers in animal care and veterinary medicine. Through volunteering, networking, and hands-on experiences, we introduce undergraduates to pathways in veterinary science and related fields. Our mission is to educate, empower, and connect students who share a genuine passion for animal welfare. We host guest speakers, organize field trips, and facilitate access to programs that provide direct animal care experience, while fostering a strong sense of community through social events and peer support.

name: PRISM Outreach
description: PRISM Outreach serves to foster a positive, inclusive, and intersectional community for queer students of all identities, providing both social and material support in the campus community.  PRISM strives to create a safe space for every individual to explore their identity and learn from the experiences of others.

name: Prison Education Project at UCI
description: The purpose of the Prison Education Project at UCI is to educate, engage, and empower the communities affected by the American Legal System and UC Irvine students to bring this social justice issue at the forefront of student conversations. As a club, we have three core values: education, social justice, and political advocacy. These values are interconnected and are a guide for our club projects, fundraising efforts, and educational material to ensure we address the United States' social and political aspects of the carceral system.

name: Pro-Health Journal Club
description: Our mission at Pro-Health Journal Club is to create a new community that serves as a platform for engaging students in different fields of STEM/Social Sciences through their mutual interest in healthcare. This will be accomplished through guiding students in their efforts to comprehend and discuss scientific journals through academic discourse, collaboration and presentations. Students will develop scientific literacy and communication skills necessary to succeed in professional/graduate schools. Strong knowledge in advanced health-related topics will be learnt and help prepare students for upper division courses and potential research labs. All UCI students who are majoring in or are simply interested in learning about at least one of the 8 different areas of healthcare are encouraged to join this community. Pro-Health Journal Club (PHC) will demonstrate the Interconnectedness of the different healthcare fields and guide its students to become informed and educated members of society who seek evidence-based knowledge.

name: Product Association at UCI
description: To foster a community of students interested in product management and related disciplines while enabling them with resources for early-career readiness.

name: Product Club at UCI
description: Our mission is to promote innovation, creativity and develop a student community of forwardthinkers, builders, and product leaders at UCI by focusing on practical learning.We are a student organization initiated by MBA students at the Paul Merage School of Businessat UCI. We got together to create a community of product leaders, bridge knowledge gaps,cultivate innovation, and help each other to launch a successful professional career.Our club facilitates networking and information sessions to better educate Merage studentsabout product management, all while introducing new and exciting career opportunities.

name: Program in Public Health Graduate Student Affairs Office
description: The mission of the public health program at the University of California Irvine is to create, integrate and disseminate population and community based knowledge to promote health and reduce the societal burden of human disease and disability through excellence in research, education, and public service.The Program in Public Health includes four academic departments for graduate study: 1. Department of Environmental and Occupational Health2. Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics3. Department of Health, Society, and Behavior4. Population Health and Disease Prevention For more information on academics, faculty, alumni, and graduate programs, please visit: https://publichealth.uci.edu/ph/_home.

name: Project Breakpoint at UCI
description: We aim to serve impoverished areas and families by providing entirely free tennis clinics, introducing children to the benefits of fitness and hobbies while tutoring and instructing them. Through mentorship and accessible athletic education, we hope to empower youth with confidence, discipline, and a lifelong appreciation for healthy recreation and community engagement.

name: Project Renegade (formerly Renegade)
description: Established in 2016, Project Renegade is a project team based at the University of California, Irvine(UCI). Composed of dancers from across the Irvine Dance Community, our mission exceedsartistic endeavors; we aspire to provide a community for dancers to immerse themselves in theart form and embrace the joy derived from dance. As a testament to our ethos, we aim to focuson the enjoyable aspects of dance: creating a space where our members can have fun andusing dance as an outlet from the stressful nature of competitive dance. Project Renegade iscommitted to upholding the essence of passion and creativity with a lively atmosphere thatfosters a sense of enjoyment for all dancers involved.

name: Project RISHI (Rural India Social and Health Improvement) at UCI
description: Project Rishi at UCI is meant to focus on the social and health improvement of rural areas in India. It is a non-profit student-led organization dedicated to promoting the sustainable development and growth of these international communities. Our mission is to advance various aspects of life quality by collaborating with local NGOs, NPOs, and community partners. Through active student involvement, we aim to combine research, innovation, and service to create meaningful change. Our members will work by organizing awareness campaigns, fundraisers, and mission trips to rural villages in India, where prepared committees focus on key areas such as clinical health, reproductive health, environmental sustainability, and computer literacy. Together we strive to create long-term, community-driven solutions that improve access to healthcare, promote education, and empower individuals through knowledge and opportunity.We also hope to encourage and promote empathy for cultural awareness and sensitivity for all UCI students, regardless of ethnicity and cultural heritage. It is an opportunity for engagement with multiple cultures, where the Asian American perspective connects to a global initiative.

name: Project Shifa at UCI
description: Project Shifa at UCI empowers immigrants, refugees, and marginalized students by expanding access to education, mentorship, wellness resources, and culturally responsive support. We work to bridge gaps in opportunity through community-centered programs that prioritize dignity, representation, and long-term growth.

name: Project Vietnam at UCI
description: The purpose of this organization is dedicated to supporting educationally and economically disadvantaged Vietnamese individuals in the Orange County area. We strive to provide unique resources and assistance including COVID-19 vaccines, mental health aid and awareness, etc. Additionally, Project Vietnam encourages medical missions to Vietnam, focusing on delivering primary, surgical, and pediatric emergency care services to those who lack access due to financial or medical barriers.

name: Promise Scholars
description: Through a collaborative effort between Student Success Initiatives (SSI) and campus partners, the Chancellor's Excellence and Promise Scholars Program aims to support the advancement and holistic development of its students. Education partnerships make up a cohort of students, consisting of first-year students and transfers, who will receive support through intentional programming and advising to meet their academic, personal, and professional needs as they make their transition into UC Irvine.

name: Psychological Science Colloquium
description: This group is used to manage colloquiums and related events organized by the Department of Psychological Science.

name: Psychological Science PhD Program
description: Students who enroll for doctoral study in the Department of Psychological Science will be welcomed into a community of scholars deeply invested in using the tools derived from psychological science to shed light on real-world problems and their solutions. In our department, we have some of the world's leading researchers studying a diverse array of issues, including the role of false memories in eye witness testimony, child maltreatment and its impact on development, socioeconomic disparities and their impact on social behavior, social anhedonia as a risk factor for psychosis, and emotional experience in older adults. This highly collaborative department is an ideal place for students interested in integrative, cutting-edge science to develop into independent thinkers. Training places a strong emphasis on evidence-based practice and our doctoral students bring with them a wealth of knowledge from their diverse educational and personal backgrounds. The educational experiences students obtain while pursuing doctoral education in our department prepares them for a variety of career paths.

name: Psychological Science with a concentration in Clinical Psychology PhD Program
description: The UCI Clinical Psychology Program follows the clinical science model. Students gain a solid foundation in research methods and data analysis as a foundation that supports learning as well as creating empirically-supported principles of assessment and intervention. The program provides students with an appreciation of the reciprocal relations between research and practice. The UCI Clinical Program is uniquely embedded within the School of Social Ecology, which emphasizes an integrative, biopsychosocial perspective on community, mental health, and physical health. Students approach clinical problems with an awareness of the complex interaction of biological, social, and community factors that influence how people interact with the environment around them.

name: Psychology Student Association
description: Psychology Student Association is an academic and social club for Psychology majors and other students interested in the field. Our mission is to offer valuable information to members in an effort to enrich each one with the knowledge and confidence to pursue a graduate education, and eventually a career in Psychology. Whether it be campus resources, internships, volunteer and research opportunities, preparedness for graduate school, a space to meet fellow students interested in the field of psychology, pursue a passion, or information about careers in Psychology and related fields, PSA strives to keep its members well informed and connected to networks of other students and faculty. We provide our members with leadership, and community service opportunities, and encourage them to become active members of the UCI community.

name: Public Health Informatics & Technology (PHIT) Program
description: UC Irvine's Public Health Informatics & Technology (PHIT) Workforce Development Program is recruiting and training the next generation of diverse public health professionals in informatics and technology skills to advance public health.The UCI PHIT program is a partnership between UCI and the Orange County Health Care Agency and the Oregon Community Health Information Network. The objectives are to (1) teach informatics and technology skills to public health undergraduate and graduate students as well as working professionals, (2) attract students from science, engineering, and other relevant disciplines to join the public health workforce, and (3) recruit and support the success of underrepresented minority students. The UCI PHIT program offers multiple undergraduate, graduate, and continuing education degrees and certificates in health informatics and technology. The PHIT Program also offers a Paid Summer Internship Program to eligible undergraduate and graduate students.

name: Public Health Mentorship Program
description: The purpose of PHMP is to build community among the Public Health undergraduates by connecting new students with continuing students to develop long-term mentor-mentee relationships.

name: Public Health Undergraduate Student Affairs Office
description: The Student Affairs team is here to provide high quality academic advising and guidance to our students, to facilitate their academic development, and to help them achieve academic, personal, and professional goals. We aim to do this in a courteous, accurate, and efficient manner.

name: Public Policy Student Association at UCI - PPSA
description: The Public Policy Student Association (PPSA) seeks to empower and equip students of UC Irvine to become the next generation of public policy experts.

name: Punjabis at UCI
description: Punjabis at UC Irvine (PAI) exists to celebrate and promote the rich heritage of Punjabi culture. Our purpose is to create a vibrant community for individuals who share a passion for Punjabi traditions, language, and values. Through a variety of events, educational programs, and cultural activities, we aim to raise awareness and foster appreciation for Punjabi culture within our community and beyond.

name: Pyo Alliance of Community Health and Education at UCI
description: Our mission is to unite premed students with a passion for community service, fostering a commitment to healthcare, volunteerism, and professional growth. Through hands-on service projects, volunteering, & public health initiatives, we strive to make a meaningful impact on underserved communities while preparing our members for careers in medicine. By combining education, outreach, and collaboration, we aim to make ourselves into compassionate future healthcare professionals dedicated to service and advocacy.

name: QT STEM
description: QT STEM is an organization at UCI for queer and/or trans people who are part of the STEM fields. With this group, we hope to create a more visible LGBTQ+ community in what can be an underrepresented area of academia. We also encourage allies to join! However, LGBTQ+ voices and experiences will be centered.  As a campus organization, we work to build support systems and connections to resources for LGBTQ+ people at the all levels of the campus community (undergraduate, graduate, postdoctoral, technicians, staff, faculty) in STEM fields. We organize weekly meetings to share and discuss topics related to the intersection of our identities and our areas of study. We also seek involvement from LGBTQ+ members of the professional community who would like to share their stories with us.

name: Quantum Computing Club at UCI
description: At the Quantum Computing Club, we’re all about unlocking the power of quantum software and building a vibrant quantum community at UCI! Whether you're a total beginner or already dreaming in qubits, we’re here to help you design, experiment, and innovate with real quantum algorithms. But we don’t stop there! We love crossing boundaries—from machine learning to optimization and beyond—exploring how quantum computing can revolutionize different fields. With hands-on projects, collabs, and a passion for the future, we’re shaping the next wave of quantum pioneers.For more information, check out our website: https://www.qc-uci.club

name: Queer & Asian at UCI - Q&A
description: Queer & Asian at UCI (Q&A) is an organization focused on the intersections of LGBTQ+, Asian, and Pacific Islander (API) identities. This group exists to engender a space, where Q&A identified individuals can share resources, find community, and peer support.

name: Raíces Dentales de UCI
description: Foster academic, professional, and personal growth through mentorship, networking, and skill-building opportunities.Promote cultural pride and representation within the dental field.Educate members about dental school preparation, community service, and oral health awareness.Collaborate with local dental professionals and organizations to provide outreach and volunteering opportunities.

name: Rang De Irvine
description: Rang De Irvine is the only Bhangra team at UCI. Bhangra is a dance that originated in Punjabi known for its very high energy and colorful performances. Our team has been around for 3 years and we have performed at competitions as far as Davis, CA and are previous reigning champions of Soulstice (UCI's annual talent show). We are open to a variety of experience levels; even if you have never tried bhangra before come join us at one of the future workshops! We are so excited to meet all of you and have you be a part of our bhangra family!

name: REACH at UCI
description: REACH at UCI's mission is to empower aspiring creators, marketers, and social media enthusiasts by connecting them with professional opportunities, and providing a space for those interested in the social media or marketing field to collaborate with one another and grow professionally.

name: ReachOut TeachOut at UCI
description: The mission of this initiative is to strengthen existing partnerships, in addition to fostering new collaborations, between high school science programs and UCI research labs. Additionally, we seek to help graduate students sharpen their science communication and teaching skills. Altogether, we hope to inspire young students to pursue careers in science, and ultimately, help to increase their preparedness for college-level study. Our vision is that these efforts will lead to the University and the scientific enterprise overall becoming more accessible to the community at large.

name: Real Estate Association at UCI- REA
description: Real Estate Association is an undergraduate student organization with the purpose of bringing together a community of students at UCI that is interested in the field of real estate. Open to all majors and backgrounds, our club provides opportunities for undergraduates to learn more about real estate, develop their leadership and professional skills, and to further their passion for service to the community. We also promote student awareness of the potential career opportunities in the field of real estate by connecting our members to professionals in different aspects of the real estate industry through a wide variety of speakers and events. REA serves to educate and connect students of UC Irvine about the Real Estate Industry and its different career and investment opportunities. Our partnership with the Center For Real Estate at UCI provides us with job/scholarship opportunities and many educational resources to provide to our members. Through our association, students have the opportunity to find successful mentors with established careers in the industry, connect with other students interested in Real Estate, learn leadership/professional skills, and further their passion for service in the community.

name: Reformed University Fellowship
description: RUF is a Christian ministry for UCI students to come and explore together who Jesus is. We want his life, death, and resurrection to shape our friendships, our thinking, and our campus.

name: Reframing Civil and Environmental Engineering at UCI - CEER
description: CEER is a coalition of undergraduate students, graduate students and postdocs from UCI CEE working to promote Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) both within our department and the university as a whole. We formed this group because we sensed a gap in the discussion and education of social, environmental, political, and economic issues within the department's curriculum, and desire to ensure that the department's Anti-Racism Task Force is making progress toward shaping a school where students feel fully represented. We are committed to working with CEE Department leadership to achieve our goals.  We strongly believe that moving towards racial justice and social equity is the responsibility of every civil and environmental engineer.

name: Regents Scholar Society at UCI
description: Regents Scholar Society at UCI is dedicated to cultivating a community of scholars who embody academic excellence, meaningful service, and transformative leadership. Through mentorship, academic resources, and leadership opportunities, we empower our members to grow, succeed, and thrive — on campus and beyond UCI — while making a lasting impact in their communities. We also strive to create a healthy, and welcoming environment for all members, and for those who are just coming into UCI.

name: Repair Cafe at UCI
description: The mission of the Repair Cafe at UCI is to provide UCI students with the opportunity to utilize their technical skills to help the local community repair their broken items, with the ultimate goal of reducing waste and promoting sustainable consumption in Orange County. This includes electronics, clothing, bicycles, furniture, and much more. UCI students will also have the opportunity to learn new skills from other volunteers through technical workshops, who bring their own diverse talents and experiences to the Repair Cafe.

name: Research Outreach at UCI
description: We are a 100% student-led, peer-support organization focused on connecting undergraduate students to research opportunities at UCI. The organization aims to support students of all majors and interests by conducting skill-based workshops and connecting with labs from all over campus. The primary goal is to introduce students to the many labs and projects at UCI and guide them in joining a lab that their interests match with. Students who are new to research will have the opportunity to navigate the field of research through peer-mentorship from Officers and other members as well as through our mentorship program. Officers will assist every student in preparing for presentations, networking opportunities, and learning the many skills essential in becoming a successful undergraduate researcher at UCI.

name: Resist US-Led War at UCI
description: The mission of Resist US-Led War at UCI is to raise the political consciousness of students at UCI around issues of militarism and build community support for those who have been impacted by US militarism.

name: REV Auto Car Club
description: As a car club at the University of California, Irvine, REV Auto Car Club aims to build a community for car enthusiasts to gather and share their collective knowledge about automobiles and motorsports. Our goals include teaching members about various aspects of automotive knowledge while constructing a network to develop strong connections in the automotive industry. We also strive to create a safe environment for car enthusiasts by promoting safe driving habits and highly discouraging street racing. REV @ UCI also gives back to the community by hosting public events, such as car shows and food drives. Using all of these resources and connections, members of REV @ UCI can become strong leaders who are extremely knowledgeable in the automotive field and enthusiastic about everything they do. Even the slightest passion for cars will not be overlooked and is all that one must possess to become a proud and capable member of REV @ UCI.

name: Right To Know Peer Educators
description: The mission of the Right to KNOW is to raise awareness throughout the UCI community about the widespread occurrence of sexual assault and to promote activities and attitudes that will contribute to the elimination of sexual violence. Central to the group's purpose is the examination of factors that contribute to sexual assault.

name: Rotaract at UC Irvine
description: Rotaract at UCI is a branch of Rotary International, an International Service Organization focused on providing aid and services to different people all over the globe. Rotaract is built with close-knit young professionals who are interested in professional development, international and community based service.

name: Rubik's Cube Club at UCI
description: The Rubik’s Cube Club at UCI aims to foster an inclusive twisty puzzle community on campus byproviding resources to collect, solve, and improve their speedcubing skills. We aim to organize WorldCube Association (WCA) competitions to make the experience accessible to the Irvine community.

name: Running Club at UCI
description: This is a club for people who enjoy running, whether it's for competitive or recreational/fitness-oriented purposes. We engage in a wide variety of running disciplines and welcome all skill levels. Social events, practices, competitions, fundraisers, volunteer events, and more will be held year-round for members to bond with each other and create their own amazing experiences!

name: Russian Club at UCI
description: Our mission is to create a supportive network for students interested in Russianlanguage and culture, facilitating connections and friendships that extend beyond theclassroom.

name: Sailing Club at UCI
description: Sailing Club at UCI will continue to compete in the local, regional, national, and international arenas of collegiate sailing. Our goal is to promote a high level of competition and the opportunity for leadership and team commitment. We also strive to preserve this program's reputation, tradition, and excellence since its founding.

name: Saturday Academy of Law at UCI School of Law
description: The Saturday Academy of Law at UCI School of Law is a pipeline program designed to introduce the legal profession and higher education to ninth-grade students from underrepresented communities. UCI undergraduate students have the opportunity to work as Teaching Assistants with the program.

name: Saudi Student Association at UCI (formerly The Saudi Students Club at UCI)
description: The mission of the Saudi Student Association encompasses two primary objectives:1- Fostering unity within our community and extending support to all our members.2- Promoting awareness and understanding of our national culture and traditions.

name: Scholars of Finance
description: Scholars of Finance seeks to prepare UCI students for their careers through self-reflection, values-based development, and mentoring with experienced professionals. We envision a world where our future business leaders distinguish right from wrong and carry themselves through their careers with righteous, principled conduct.

name: Scholarship Opportunities Program
description: The Scholarship Opportunities Program (SOP) works toward UCI's mission to encourage high-achieving undergraduates to compete successfully for the most prestigious scholarships, grants, and graduate fellowships available, and to begin learning about the process as early as possible. In the Division of Undergraduate Education under the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning, SOP organizes and disseminates information on a select group of prestigious awards that are national and international in scope, including opportunities for funded research and study at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. SOP facilitates UCI's processes for evaluating applications and endorsing candidates for awards requiring University nomination. Additionally, SOP provides individual and group counseling, presents workshops, assists students with curriculum vitae (CVs), and edits Statements of Purpose and research/project proposals, and strengthen interviewing skills.

name: School of Education
description: The UCI School of Education mission is to improve access to high-quality educational opportunities for all individuals in our university, community and beyond. We are dedicated to producing responsive and innovative cutting-edge research, program design and a next generation of educators that will contribute to a transformational shift in education. We are committed to ensuring that all students are empowered and prepared to lead successful and productive lives and careers in a democratic society.

name: School of Education Student Affairs Office
description: The School of Education's Office of Student Affairs provides student-centered educational support and resources to empower undergraduate and graduate students within the School of Education to achieve academic and personal success.

name: School of Education | Ph.D. in Education
School of Engineering - Graduate and Professional Studies
description: The UCI Samueli School of Engineering educates more than 4,600 students with an integrative approach that blends fundamentals, research and hands-on experience. The school's aim is to unleash innovation, create opportunities and inspire ingenuity. The Samueli School's faculty members are leaders in their disciplines who have achieved worldwide recognition for their research and dedicated teaching. The school offers both research based and experiential professional masters programs. The school pursues research and education that is timely, socially responsible and cutting edge, and works in partnership with industry and state and federal agencies to promote the transfer of research to applications that benefit society.

name: School of Humanities Office of Undergraduate Study
description: Academic Advising Office for the School of Humanities

name: School of Law
description: Let's Go Change the World

name: School of Pharmacy & Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: Be a driving force for advancing health and wellness of individuals and society, through innovative and integrative learner-centered education; cutting-edge pharmaceutical research and discoveries; and leadership in inter-professional patient-centered healthcare.

name: School of Physical Sciences
description: Our aim is to deliver scientific breakthroughs that reshape our understanding of the physical world and provide solutions to the most profound problems of our age.  We achieve this by asking hard questions; setting inspiring, visionary goals; and cultivating an inclusive, interdisciplinary culture that is open to broad ideas.

name: School of Social Ecology
description: Science-driving solutions
